    Mumbai spice exporter reroutes around a disrupted port

    A Mumbai spice exporter is due to ship to a verified buyer in Kuwait when a route alert warns of severe congestion and disruption on its usual transshipment route. Through T57 it requests new quotes and is matched with a vetted forwarder offering an alternative routing through a different hub. It books in one step, the buyer sees the new plan and arrival date on the trade record, and the goods arrive within the contract window.

    We believe that reliable logistics should be available to every food business, not only the largest shippers.

    Every logistics partner is checked before joining and rated on recorded performance.

    T57 does not move cargo

    Transport, storage and handling are provided by partners. T57 matches, books and records.

    Partners go through business verification, licence and insurance checks, and their performance is rated on recorded shipments.

    Can I invite my own forwarder?

    Yes. Your existing forwarder can join the trade record and quote alongside network partners.

    Does T57 negotiate freight rates?

    T57 aggregates demand and shows comparable quotes, which helps members get competitive rates. Members choose and book.

    Capabilities · Logistics and Fulfilment · Tracking

    Where your food is. What state it is in.

    Know where your food is, what condition it is in and when it will arrive.

    Track your next shipment on T57See how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. LocationWithout T57: Separate carrier portalsWith T57: One live view
    2. ProblemsWithout T57: Found on arrivalWith T57: Alerts in transit
    3. EvidenceWithout T57: WeakWith T57: Tamper-evident log

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 solves the blind spots between shipment and delivery, by bringing location, milestones and temperature data for every shipment onto one trade record that buyer, seller, lender and insurer can all see.

    The problem

    Blind spots between shipment and delivery

    Once food leaves the warehouse, most businesses lose sight of it. Updates come by email from forwarders, carrier websites show different information, and temperature problems are discovered only when a container is opened. Buyers cannot plan, sellers cannot reassure them, and lenders and insurers have no independent evidence of what happened. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    No single view

    Tracking information is spread across carriers, forwarders and ports.

    Late discovery of problems

    Delays and temperature breaches are found too late to act.

    Weak evidence

    Without recorded data, claims and disputes are hard to settle.

    How T57 works for you

    Connect the shipment → Follow it live → Monitor condition → Act on alerts

    1. 01

      Connect the shipment

      Booking references, container numbers and tracking devices are linked to the trade record.

    2. 02

      Follow it live

      See location, estimated arrival and milestones such as loading, departure, transshipment and arrival.

    3. 03

      Monitor condition

      For reefer cargo, temperature and humidity readings stream to the record.

    4. 04

      Act on alerts

      Delays, route changes and temperature breaches trigger alerts to the right people, and milestones can trigger payments.

    Features

    9 features, one trade record

    Multi-carrier trackingSea, air and road shipments in one view. For importers, this ends checking several websites.
    Milestone timelineLoading, departure, transshipment, arrival, customs release and delivery. For buyers, this supports planning.
    Predicted arrivalAI estimates arrival times from live and historical data. For distributors, this improves warehouse and sales planning.
    Temperature and humidity monitoringLive readings from reefer containers and IoT devices. For meat, seafood, dairy and fresh produce, this protects quality.
    Smart alertsNotifications for delays, route changes and condition breaches. For operations teams, this means acting before it is too late.
    Shared visibilityBuyer, seller, lender and insurer see the same data, based on their permissions. For everyone, this means fewer status emails.
    Milestone-triggered paymentsArrival or delivery can release escrow payments automatically. For sellers, this speeds up cash.
    Tamper-evident logKey tracking events are anchored on the ledger. For insurers, this makes claims evidence reliable.
    Proof of deliveryDigital delivery confirmation with photos and signatures. For both sides, this closes the trade cleanly.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    Chittagong importer spots a reefer fault before it spoils a shipment

    A Chittagong importer is bringing frozen chicken from a verified Brazilian processor. During transshipment, T57 alerts the importer and the processor that the container's temperature is rising. The forwarder is notified on the same record and has the reefer unit repaired at the port within hours. The cargo arrives in good condition, and the temperature log shows the buyer and insurer exactly what happened.

    Why T57

    We believe that everyone with a stake in a shipment deserves the same, reliable picture.

    One version of events

    Tracking data sits on the same record as the contract, documents and payments.

    AI advises, people decide

    AI predicts arrival times and flags risks. People decide how to respond.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Do I need special tracking devices?

    No. T57 uses carrier and port data for all shipments. IoT devices add live temperature and location for sensitive cargo.

    Who can see my shipment?

    Only the parties to the trade and the partners you authorize, such as your lender or insurer.

    Can tracking trigger payment?

    Yes. Agreed milestones, such as arrival or delivery confirmation, can release escrow payments automatically.

    Capabilities · Logistics and Fulfilment · Customs

    Documents prepared once. Clearance faster.

    Prepare export and import documents once, and clear food through customs faster.

    Prepare your next export documents on T57See how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. DocumentsWithout T57: InconsistentWith T57: Generated from the trade
    2. HS codesWithout T57: ErrorsWith T57: Guided classification
    3. SubmissionWithout T57: LateWith T57: Sent ahead for pre-clearance

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 solves the document errors and border delays that hold perishable food at ports, by preparing customs documents from the trade record and sending them ahead for pre-clearance where authorities support it.

    The problem

    Perishable food held at the port

    Food crossing a border needs a stack of documents: commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, health, phytosanitary and halal certificates, import permits and the customs declaration. Each must match the others exactly. One wrong HS code, weight or date can hold a container for days, and for chilled or frozen food every day costs money and quality. The WTO estimated that full implementation of its Trade Facilitation Agreement could cut trade costs by an average of 14.3% (WTO, World Trade Report 2015). Much of that saving comes from simpler, digital border procedures. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Inconsistent documents

    The same data is typed into many documents by different parties, creating mismatches.

    Classification errors

    Wrong HS codes lead to delays, penalties or the wrong duty.

    Late submission

    Documents reach customs only when the goods arrive, so clearance starts late.

    How T57 works for you

    Documents on record → Sent before arrival → Pre-cleared → Sample and release

    1. 01

      Documents on record

      Commercial documents are generated from the contract, and certificates are added by issuers and partners.

    2. 02

      Sent before arrival

      The complete, checked document set goes to the customs broker and, where supported, to the authority before the goods arrive.

    3. 03

      Pre-cleared

      Authorities can review and risk-assess the shipment in advance.

    4. 04

      Sample and release

      On arrival, any required inspection or sampling takes place and the goods are released faster.

    Features

    9 features, one trade record

    Document generationCommercial invoice, packing list and other trade documents built from the contract. For exporters, this means data entered once.
    HS code guidanceAI suggests HS codes from product descriptions and past classifications, for broker or member confirmation. For new exporters, this reduces classification errors.
    Market requirementsLists of the documents and certificates each destination needs for each product. For first-time exporters, this means nothing is missed.
    Certificate managementHealth, phytosanitary, halal and origin certificates linked to the right shipment. For inspectors and customs, this means easy checks.
    Consistency checksAI compares every document for mismatched weights, values, dates and descriptions. For importers, this prevents holds at the port.
    Customs broker networkVetted brokers in T57's markets file declarations from the trade record. For members, this means reliable local expertise.
    Paperless pre-clearanceDocuments sent ahead to authorities that support pre-arrival processing. For perishable cargo, this cuts dwell time.
    Duty and tax estimatesEstimates of duties and taxes before shipment. For buyers, this means landed costs without surprises.
    Document vaultEvery document stored on the tamper-evident trade record. For audits and disputes, this is a complete archive.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    Antalya fresh-produce exporter clears goods in Riyadh ahead of arrival

    An exporter of fresh peppers and tomatoes in Antalya ships by road to a verified Riyadh wholesaler. The invoice and packing list are generated from the contract, and the phytosanitary certificate and certificate of origin are added to the trade record. AI checks flag a weight mismatch, which is corrected before departure. The vetted customs broker lodges the documents before the truck reaches the border, and the goods are released after a routine check.

    Why T57

    We believe that food should spend its time on shelves, not at the border.

    Built for regulators too

    Complete, consistent, tamper-evident records support customs authorities and make paperless pre-clearance possible.

    AI advises, people decide

    AI suggests HS codes and flags errors. Brokers and members confirm, and customs authorities decide.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Does T57 file customs declarations?

    No. Licensed customs brokers file declarations, using the documents prepared on T57.

    Is pre-clearance available in every country?

    Pre-clearance depends on each customs authority's procedures. Where it is not available, T57 still sends complete, checked documents to the broker before arrival.

    Are AI-suggested HS codes final?

    No. They are suggestions for a broker or member to confirm. The final classification is the declarant's responsibility.

    TodayWith T57

    T57 solves the information gap between large trading houses and everyone else, by building price, supply, credit and trade data into the platform where food is bought and sold.

    The problem

    Trading houses see more than everyone else

    Food prices are rising again. The FAO Food Price Index averaged 136.0 points in September 2026, up 5.8% on a year earlier (FAO, October 2026) and at its highest level since late 2022. Large traders follow these moves with paid terminals and analyst teams. Most food SMEs rely on calls, rumors and last month's invoices. They quote too low, buy too late, choose counterparties without checking their history and enter new markets blind. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Pricing blind

    No reliable, current price for the products and origins being traded.

    Unknown counterparties

    No easy way to check a buyer's or supplier's credit and trade history.

    Missed signals

    Supply shocks and demand shifts are seen only after they hit.

    How T57 works for you

    Watch → Check → Prepare → Act

    1. 01

      Watch

      Follow prices, supply status and forecasts for the products and markets you trade.

    2. 02

      Check

      Look up a counterparty's credit report and trade history before you commit.

    3. 03

      Prepare

      Use AI negotiation support to set target prices and positions from market data.

    4. 04

      Act

      Quote, buy, hedge your timing or switch origin, without leaving the platform.

    01Live Food Price IndexPrices by product, grade and origin from public markets and anonymized, aggregated T57 trades.02AI Negotiations EngineAI that prepares negotiating positions, benchmarks offers and suggests counter-offers, with people deciding.03Supply and demand forecastingAI forecasts of price, supply and demand by product and market.
    04Trade data servicesCredit reports, port trade history and HS code guidance for counterparties and markets.
    05Food security viewSupply status by origin (surplus, stable, at risk, shortage) for governments and institutions.

    A Dubai sugar trader sees on T57's price index that refined sugar prices have started rising, and the forecast points to tighter supply. A new supplier in Brazil offers a competitive price. The trader checks its credit report and port trade history on T57, uses AI negotiation support to set a counter-offer based on recent trades, and closes the deal before prices climb further.

    Why T57

    We believe that better information should not be a privilege of the largest traders.

    Data from real trade

    Price and supply data combine public sources with anonymized, aggregated T57 trades. No individual member's prices are ever shared.

    AI advises, people decide

    Forecasts, benchmarks and suggestions inform your decisions. They never make them for you.

    Common questions

    Where does T57's data come from?

    Public market and trade sources, licensed data partners, and anonymized, aggregated data from trades on T57.

    Is my trade data shared with other members?

    No. Individual trades are never shown. They contribute only to anonymized, aggregated statistics.

    Is intelligence included in membership?

    Core intelligence is included. Higher membership tiers include deeper data, credit reports and forecasts.

    Capabilities · Intelligence and Data · Price Index

    Today's food prices, from real trades.

    Current food prices by product, grade and origin, built from real trades.

    Explore the T57 Food Price IndexSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. Your productWithout T57: No reliable priceWith T57: Priced by grade and origin
    2. FreshnessWithout T57: Out of dateWith T57: Updated with verified trades
    3. FairnessWithout T57: Unequal informationWith T57: The same view for every member

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 solves the lack of reliable, current prices for the food products SMEs actually trade, by combining public market data with anonymized prices from verified trades on T57.

    The problem

    No current price for what you actually trade

    Global benchmarks such as the FAO Food Price Index show the big picture: the index averaged 136.0 points in September 2026, up 5.8% year on year (FAO, October 2026). But a date exporter in Madinah or a rice importer in Kuala Lumpur needs to know the price of a specific grade, from a specific origin, delivered to a specific market, this week. Exchange prices cover only a few commodities, and most food is priced through private deals that leave no public trace. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    No price for your product

    Many food products have no exchange or public benchmark.

    Out-of-date information

    Prices from contacts or old invoices lag the market.

    Unequal information

    The other side of the deal often knows the market better than you do.

    How T57 works for you

    Choose your products → See current prices → Compare offers → Get alerts

    1. 01

      Choose your products

      Select products, grades, origins and destinations to follow.

    2. 02

      See current prices

      View the T57 index, recent price ranges and trends, updated as new data arrives.

    3. 03

      Compare offers

      See every quote and bid on T57 alongside the index.

    4. 04

      Get alerts

      Be notified when prices move beyond the thresholds you set.

    Features

    10 features, one trade record

    Product-level indexPrices by product, grade, packaging and origin, not just broad categories. For traders, this matches how food is really sold.
    Blended sourcesPublic market data, licensed data partners and anonymized, aggregated T57 trades. For members, this gives a fuller picture.
    Trade-weighted updatesThe index updates as verified trades close on the platform. For buyers, this means current prices.
    Price ranges and trendsLow, high and median, with history. For category managers, this shows where the market is heading.
    Quote benchmarkingEvery quote and bid shown against the index. For both sides, this supports fair negotiation.
    Price alertsNotifications when prices cross your thresholds. For importers, this supports better timing.
    Landed-cost viewCombine product price with freight, insurance and duty estimates. For buyers, this shows the true cost by origin.
    AI price signalsAI flags unusual moves and links them to known events, such as export bans or route closures. For traders, this explains the move.
    Embeddable widgetA public version of selected index lines for the T57 homepage and partners. For the market, this improves transparency.
    Privacy by designNo individual member's prices are ever shown. For members, this protects commercial confidentiality.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    Kuala Lumpur rice importer negotiates with confidence

    A Kuala Lumpur rice importer receives quotes for 1121 basmati from three verified Indian exporters. On T57, each quote is shown against the price index for that grade and origin, delivered to Port Klang. One quote is well above the index range and another is suspiciously low. The importer asks the high bidder to revise, checks the low bidder's track record, and awards the contract at a fair, market-based price.

    Why T57

    We believe that a fair price starts with a shared, trustworthy reference.

    Built from verified trades

    Platform prices come from trades between verified members, not from unverified listings.

    AI advises, people decide

    AI explains price moves and flags outliers. People decide what to pay or charge.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    How is the T57 index calculated?

    It combines public market data, licensed data partners and anonymized, aggregated prices from verified T57 trades, with methods that prevent any single member's price from being identified.

    How often is it updated?

    It updates as new market data arrives and as verified trades close on T57. Some lines update daily, others weekly, depending on trade volume.

    Can non-members see the index?

    A selection of index lines is public on the T57 website. Full detail, history and alerts are available to members.

    Capabilities · Intelligence and Data · AI Negotiations

    Negotiate with data and AI behind you.

    Negotiate every food deal with market data and AI preparation behind you.

    See AI negotiation support in a demoSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. InformationWithout T57: UnequalWith T57: Market data on every offer
    2. PreparationWithout T57: RushedWith T57: An AI brief before you start
    3. DecisionsWithout T57: Made without dataWith T57: Always yours, with data

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 solves the information imbalance in food negotiations, by giving every member AI that prepares positions, benchmarks offers and suggests counter-offers, while people make every decision.

    The problem

    The other side knows more than you

    In many food deals, one side knows the market far better than the other. Large buyers have category teams and price data. Small exporters and first-time importers negotiate on instinct, often accepting the first offer or losing a deal by pushing too hard. Negotiations also happen across email and messaging apps, so terms get lost and nobody can see how the final deal compares with the market. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Unequal information

    One party negotiates with data, the other without.

    Poor preparation

    There is no time to research prices, costs and alternatives before every negotiation.

    Scattered terms

    Price is negotiated in one place, while payment, delivery and quality terms are negotiated somewhere else.

    How T57 works for you

    Prepare → Set your position → Negotiate → Decide and close

    1. 01

      Prepare

      Before you respond to a quote or RFQ, the engine summarizes the market price, your costs, the counterparty's history and your alternatives.

    2. 02

      Set your position

      It suggests a target, an opening offer and a walk-away point, which you can adjust.

    3. 03

      Negotiate

      As offers move back and forth on T57, the engine benchmarks each one and suggests counter-offers, covering price, payment terms, Incoterms and delivery.

    4. 04

      Decide and close

      You accept, counter or walk away. The agreed terms become the contract.

    Features

    9 features, one trade record

    Pre-negotiation briefA summary of the market price, recent trades, counterparty history and alternatives. For SMEs, this means walking in prepared.
    Target and walk-away suggestionsData-based ranges you can adjust. For exporters, this protects margins.
    Offer benchmarkingEvery offer compared with the price index and similar trades. For buyers, this shows when a price is out of line.
    Counter-offer suggestionsSuggested responses with the reasoning shown. For new traders, this builds confidence.
    Whole-deal viewPrice weighed with payment terms, Incoterms, delivery dates and quality specifications. For both sides, this means better total value, not just price.
    Scenario comparisonCompare the value of different combinations of price, payment and delivery terms. For finance teams, this clarifies trade-offs.
    Multilingual supportHelp in Arabic, English, Hindi, Malay, Turkish and more. For cross-border deals, this reduces misunderstandings.
    Negotiation recordEvery offer and counter-offer is recorded on the trade record. For disputes, this shows exactly what was agreed.
    Human controlThe engine never sends an offer or accepts a deal on its own. For members, this means you are always in charge.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    Hyderabad poultry exporter wins better payment terms in Oman

    A frozen poultry exporter in Hyderabad receives an offer from a verified Muscat distributor at a price slightly below the index, with 90-day payment terms. The engine's brief shows the price is fair, but that the long payment terms reduce the deal's real value. It suggests accepting the price in return for escrow with 50% on shipment. The exporter makes that counter-offer, the distributor agrees, and the terms flow straight into the contract.

    Why T57

    We believe that a good negotiation is one where both sides understand the market.

    AI advises, people decide

    The engine prepares, benchmarks and suggests. It never negotiates, sends offers or accepts deals without a person's decision.

    Fair to both sides

    Both parties can use the engine, and it draws only on anonymized, aggregated market data. It never uses the other party's private information.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Does the AI negotiate on my behalf?

    No. It prepares and suggests. You decide what to offer, counter or accept, and nothing is sent without your confirmation.

    Can the other side see the engine's suggestions to me?

    No. Your briefs and suggestions are private to you.

    What data does the engine use?

    The T57 price index, anonymized and aggregated trade data, the counterparty's public T57 profile and track record, and your own costs and history if you choose to add them.

    Rent the equipment you cannot afford to own.

    Rent tractors, harvesters, cold storage and processing equipment when you need it.

    Find equipment near youSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. CostWithout T57: Too high to ownWith T57: Rent when needed
    2. TimingWithout T57: Unavailable at harvestWith T57: Booked by date and place
    3. OwnersWithout T57: Idle machinesWith T57: Earning from rentals

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 solves the high cost of owning farm and food equipment, by connecting farmers, cooperatives and processors with verified owners who rent out machinery, cold storage and processing capacity.

    The problem

    Equipment too costly to own, idle when owned

    Small farms produce around a third of the world's food (FAO, 2021), but few smallholders can afford to buy a tractor, harvester or cold room that they use only a few weeks a year. Without the right equipment at the right time, harvests are late, quality drops and more food is lost. Meanwhile, equipment owners, from larger farms to service companies, have machines standing idle for much of the year. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Unaffordable equipment

    Buying machinery is out of reach for most small farmers and cooperatives.

    Bad timing

    Without equipment at harvest, crops are picked late or lost.

    Idle assets

    Equipment owners lack a trusted way to rent machines to people they do not know.

    How T57 works for you

    Search → Book → Use → Pay and review

    1. 01

      Search

      Find equipment by type, location and dates, from tractors and harvesters to cold rooms and packing lines.

    2. 02

      Book

      Compare verified owners, prices and availability, then book with terms and deposit agreed on T57.

    3. 03

      Use

      Collect the equipment or have an operator come with it, with handover condition recorded.

    4. 04

      Pay and review

      Pay through escrow, return the equipment and rate the rental.

    Features

    10 features, one trade record

    Wide equipment rangeTractors, harvesters, sprayers, irrigation, cold rooms, reefer containers, graders and packing lines. For farmers and processors, this means one place to find what they need.
    Verified owners and rentersBoth sides hold T57 Passports. For owners, this reduces the risk of renting to strangers.
    Location and date searchFind equipment near you for the dates you need. For growers, this matches the harvest calendar.
    Operator optionsRent with or without a trained operator. For smallholders, this removes the need for skills they lack.
    Escrow payments and depositsPayments and deposits held by licensed partners. For both sides, this means fair settlement.
    Condition recordsPhotos and checklists at handover and return. For owners, this settles damage disputes.
    Equipment insuranceCover arranged through licensed partners. For owners, this protects their assets.
    Cooperative bookingCooperatives can book equipment on behalf of their members. For FPOs, this shares costs fairly.
    Linked to contract farmingRentals can be planned against contract farming schedules and financed with input finance. For buyers, this protects supply quality.
    Ratings and historyReviews from recorded rentals. For everyone, this rewards reliable owners and renters.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    Punjab farmer cooperative rents harvesters for the wheat season

    A farmer producer organization in Punjab needs combine harvesters for a two-week wheat harvest window. On T57 it finds two verified owners nearby and books both machines with operators. Payment and a deposit are held in escrow by a licensed partner. Condition is recorded at handover, the harvest is completed on time, and the cooperative's buyer, under a contract farming agreement, receives grain at the agreed quality.

    Why T57

    We believe that the right tools at the right time should not depend on how much land you own.

    Verified on both sides

    Owners and renters are verified T57 members, and every rental is recorded.

    Connected to the food chain

    Equipment rental links to contract farming, input finance and buyers on the same platform.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Can I list my equipment for rent?

    Yes. Verified members can list equipment, set prices and availability, and choose who can rent it.

    Who is responsible if equipment is damaged?

    The rental terms, condition records and any insurance set out responsibility. Disputes are handled under those terms and the payment partner's rules.

    Is equipment rental available everywhere?

    It starts in T57's founding markets and grows as owners join in each region.

    What you get with T57 AI

    1. ExpertiseWithout T57: Only for the largest playersWith T57: An AI trade desk for every member
    2. ModelsWithout T57: Generic, globalWith T57: Small, local, food-trained
    3. DecisionsWithout T57: Black boxesWith T57: Explained, reviewed by people

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 builds AI into every step of food trade, from matching and pricing to compliance, forecasting and documents, so every member gets expert support, and people still make every decision.

    The problem

    Food trade still runs on calls, spreadsheets and guesswork

    Most food trade still runs on phone calls, spreadsheets and experience. Buyers search for suppliers by word of mouth. Prices are guessed from last month's deals. Documents are typed by hand and checked by eye. Farmers plant without knowing what the market will want. General-purpose AI tools do not help much, because they know little about a basmati grade in Punjab, a date harvest in Al-Ahsa or the documents a Malaysian importer needs. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Expertise only the largest players can afford

    Market analysts, compliance teams and trade specialists are out of reach for most food SMEs.

    Generic AI that does not know food

    Large global models lack local crop, market and regulatory knowledge, and often lack local languages.

    AI no one can check

    Black-box decisions about credit, compliance or pricing are hard to trust.

    How we prove it

    What we measure, and publish with dates

    Every model is measured on real T57 trade data. These are the results we track and will publish, by market and crop, with the date of each measurement.

    • Matching acceptance rate
    • Forecast error by crop and market

    Use case · Illustrative example

    Jeddah importer, before and after T57 AI

    Before

    A Jeddah food importer found suppliers through agents, checked prices by phone and had its staff type every document. A sanctions issue with one supplier was discovered only when the bank stopped the payment.

    With T57 AI

    On T57, AI suggests verified suppliers, benchmarks each quote against the price index, screens every counterparty before the deal, drafts documents from the contract and flags supply risks weeks ahead. The importer's team spends its time deciding, not searching and typing.

    Why T57 AI

    We believe that AI in food trade must be useful, local and accountable.

    AI advises, people decideNo credit, compliance or membership decision against a member is made by AI alone. Every adverse decision is reviewed by a person and can be explained.
    Responsible by designT57's AI governance is built around the risk-based principles of the EU AI Act and the ISO/IEC 42001 standard for AI management systems: documented models, tested data, human oversight and regular review.
    Local knowledge, with consentFarmer knowledge is recorded only with consent, and farmers stay credited for what they contribute.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    What does "AI-native" mean at T57?

    AI is built into every step of the trade, from matching and pricing to compliance and documents, rather than added as a separate tool.

    Does AI make decisions about my business?

    AI makes suggestions and flags issues. People make decisions, and every adverse decision is reviewed by a person.

    What data does T57's AI use?

    Verified trade records, public market, trade and climate data, licensed data from partners, and farmer knowledge recorded with consent. Individual members' data is never shared with other members.

    Why small, local models?

    Food is global but hyper-local. Small models trained for a region, crop and value chain understand local conditions and languages better, cost less to run and are easier to test and explain.

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's matchmaking AI solves the slow, contact-driven search for trading partners, by ranking verified members against each request on product, capacity, corridor, compliance and past performance.

    The problem without AI

    Why this is hard without AI

    Food businesses find partners through agents, trade fairs, old contacts and directories full of unverified listings. A buyer may spend weeks finding a supplier who can deliver the right grade, in the right volume, to the right port, and still not know whether that supplier is the producer or one more intermediary. Sellers miss buyers in markets they have never sold to. Good matches exist, but nobody can see them.

    How the AI works

    Data in, a small local model, a person decides

    Model typeA ranking model that combines product and specification matching (using language embeddings of product descriptions) with learned scores for fit and reliability. Regional models handle local product names and grades.
    Data inputsThe RFQ or offer (product, grade, volume, packaging, Incoterms, destination, timing). Member profiles, role labels and verified capacity. Corridor and logistics data. Compliance status. The outcomes of past trades, such as completion, on-time delivery and disputes.
    OutputA ranked shortlist of verified counterparties, each with the reasons it was suggested, such as "owner-producer, ships to Jeddah monthly, 98% on-time on T57". The member chooses whom to invite.

    See it in the trade flow: RFQ & Trade Execution

    What it delivers

    Faster sourcing · Better matches · New markets

    Faster sourcing

    A shortlist of suitable, verified partners in minutes instead of weeks.

    Better matches

    Ranking on specification, capacity, corridor and track record, not just keywords.

    New markets

    Sellers are surfaced to buyers in markets they could not reach through their own contacts.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    Selangor snack manufacturer finds a new date paste supplier

    Before

    A snack manufacturer in Selangor spent six weeks calling agents to find a new date paste supplier after its usual source fell short, and still could not confirm who made the product.

    With T57 AI

    It posts an RFQ on T57, and matchmaking ranks five verified suppliers in Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Two are labelled owner-producer, with halal certificates and recent shipments to Malaysia. It invites three, receives bids within days and awards the contract to a producer in Qassim.

    Why T57 AI

    Validated, verified and accountable

    Validated on real outcomesMatching is measured by whether suggested partners are invited, win and complete trades on time. Results are reviewed regularly and published by market.
    Verified data onlyThe model ranks only verified members and learns from recorded trade outcomes, not from unverified listings or paid placement.
    AI advises, people decideThe AI suggests and explains. Members choose whom to invite and deal with.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Can suppliers pay to rank higher?

    No. Ranking is based on fit, verification and track record, never on payment.

    Why was a particular partner suggested?

    Every suggestion shows its main reasons, such as product match, capacity, corridor experience and on-time performance.

    The problem without AI

    A small exporter facing a large importer often does not know the going price for its grade, what longer payment terms really cost, or how far it can push. Many accept the first offer.     How the AI works

    OutputA private brief with the market range, a suggested target, opening and walk-away points, the value of each term (price, payment days, Incoterms, delivery) and suggested counter-offers, with reasons. Nothing is sent without your confirmation.

    Kayseri dried apricot exporter values payment terms correctly

    A dried apricot exporter in Kayseri accepted a Dubai buyer's offer at a good price, without realizing that 120-day payment terms wiped out most of its margin once financing costs were counted.

    With T57 AI

    On T57, the brief shows the offer's price is above the market median, but the payment terms reduce its real value below the index. The engine suggests a counter-offer at a slightly lower price with escrow released on arrival. The buyer agrees, and the exporter's margin is protected.

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's price AI solves the missing prices for most traded food, by estimating current prices from scattered market data and verified trades, and explaining why they move.

    The problem without AI

    Why this is hard without AI

    Global benchmarks track the big picture: the FAO Food Price Index averaged 136.0 points in September 2026, up 5.8% on a year earlier (FAO, October 2026). But most food is sold through private deals, in hundreds of grades and pack sizes, with no public price. Data that does exist is patchy, uses different units and currencies, and arrives late. Without AI, building a reliable price for "medjool dates, large, 5 kg cartons, delivered to Kuala Lumpur" is close to impossible.

    How the AI works

    Data in, a small local model, a person decides

    Model typeStatistical and machine-learning models that clean, normalize and combine price signals, estimate prices where trades are sparse, and detect unusual moves. A language model writes plain-language explanations.
    Data inputsPublic market and exchange data. Licensed data partners. Anonymized, aggregated prices from verified T57 trades. Freight and currency rates. News and policy events such as export bans and route closures.
    OutputA price and range for each product, grade, origin and destination, a confidence level, recent trends, and a short explanation of significant moves.

    See it in the trade flow: Live Food Price Index

    What it delivers

    Prices where none existed · Faster signals · Explained moves

    Prices where none existed

    Estimates for products and grades with no public benchmark, each with a confidence level.

    Faster signals

    Updates as new trades close and new data arrives.

    Explained moves

    Members see why prices change, not just that they changed.

    Madinah date exporter prices a new market

    Before

    A Madinah date exporter priced its first offer to a Malaysian buyer from a two-month-old quote and undercut itself.

    With T57 AI

    T57 shows an estimated delivered price range for its grade and pack in Kuala Lumpur, with medium confidence and a note that prices are rising ahead of Ramadan. The exporter quotes within the range and wins the order at a better margin.

    Why T57 AI

    Validated, verified and accountable

    Back-tested and transparentEstimates are checked against prices from later verified trades, and every price shows its confidence level.
    Private by designIndividual members' prices are never shown. They feed only anonymized, aggregated estimates.
    AI advises, people decideThe index informs pricing. Members set their own prices.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    How accurate are the AI estimates?

    Each price shows a confidence level. Accuracy is measured by comparing estimates with later verified trades, and results are published by product group.

    Can the index be manipulated by fake trades?

    Only trades between verified members count, outliers are detected and down-weighted, and no single trade can move the index alone.

    Why this is hard without AI

    Food supply shocks rarely come without warning, but the signals are scattered: weather, planting data, export policies, freight disruption and shifting demand. When the Strait of Hormuz closed in 2026, urea prices rose about 80% between February and April (World Bank, May 2026), with knock-on effects for the next harvests. Large traders and governments model these signals. Most food businesses learn about them only when prices jump or orders fail.

    How the AI works

    Data in, a small local model, a person decides

    Model typeTime-series and machine-learning forecasting models, with small regional models for each crop and market, combined into supply status signals.
    Data inputsHistorical prices and trade flows. Weather and climate data. Planting, yield and crop-condition data. Input costs such as fertilizer. Export and import policies. Freight and route disruption. Demand indicators such as seasonal and religious calendars. Anonymized T57 trade and RFQ activity.
    OutputForecasts of price, supply and demand by product, origin and market, with ranges. A supply status for each origin (surplus, stable, at risk or shortage), and alerts when the outlook changes.

    What it delivers

    Earlier action · Better planning · Food security insight

    Earlier action

    Buyers can switch origins or buy forward before shortages bite.

    Better planning

    Sellers and processors can plan volumes, storage and sales.

    Food security insight

    Governments and institutions see risks to supply early, through T57's food security view.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    Abu Dhabi food distributor secures rice ahead of a shortage

    Before

    An Abu Dhabi distributor learned of an export restriction on its main rice origin only when its supplier cancelled, and paid a premium for emergency stock.

    With T57 AI

    T57 moves that origin from stable to at risk three weeks earlier, on weak monsoon data and policy signals, and forecasts rising prices. The distributor sends RFQs to verified suppliers in two other origins and secures supply for the next quarter before prices rise.

    Why T57 AI

    Validated, verified and accountable

    Validated against what happenedForecasts are back-tested and tracked against actual prices and volumes, and error ranges are shown with every forecast.
    Local models for local marketsSmall models for each region and crop capture local seasons, policies and conditions.
    AI advises, people decideForecasts inform decisions. They never make them.

    How far ahead do forecasts look?

    From a few weeks to a season, depending on the product and the data available. Every forecast shows its range.

    Can governments use the forecasts?

    Yes. Governments and institutions can access aggregated supply status and forecasts through T57's food security view.

    The problem without AI

    Why this is hard without AI

    A single food trade can fail for many reasons: a buyer in financial trouble, a sanctioned owner, a port strike, a closed strait, a drought or a sudden export ban. Each risk is tracked, if at all, by a different person in a different place. Lenders and insurers price risk without seeing the trade. Governments see supply threats only after they become shortages. Without a combined view, risks are found too late to act on.

    How the AI works

    Data in, a small local model, a person decides

    Model typeRisk-scoring models for counterparties, corridors and origins, plus event detection from news and data feeds. Results are aggregated into geographic and portfolio heatmaps.
    Data inputsVerified member data and trade history on T57. Compliance screening results. Credit data from partners, with consent. Port, shipping and route data. Weather and climate data. Export and import policy changes. Supply status forecasts.
    OutputRisk scores with the main reasons behind them, heatmaps by region, product and route, and alerts when a risk rises above a set level.

    One view of risk · Early warning · Better pricing and protection

    One view of risk

    Counterparty, route, market and climate risk together, for each trade or portfolio.

    Early warning

    Alerts as risks rise, not after losses happen.

    The problem without AI

    Why this is hard without AI

    Many farmers and small food businesses only find out whether a season or a deal made money when it is over. Input costs move fast, as fertilizer prices did after the 2026 Hormuz closure, when urea prices rose about 80% in two months (World Bank, May 2026). Prices at harvest are uncertain, and hidden costs such as freight, finance, losses and payment delays erode margins. Decisions about what to plant, which contract to sign or which buyer to choose are made without a clear view of profit.

    How the AI works

    Data in, a small local model, a person decides

    Model typeScenario models that combine yield forecasts, price forecasts and cost models, with Monte Carlo simulation to show the range of likely outcomes.
    Data inputsCrop and yield forecasts. Price index and price forecasts. Input costs (seed, fertilizer, labor, water, equipment rental). Freight, insurance and finance costs. Contract terms and payment timing. The member's own costs, if added.
    OutputExpected profit or loss with a likely range, the main drivers of margin, a break-even price, and side-by-side comparisons of scenarios such as different crops, contracts or buyers.

    What it delivers

    Smarter choices · Fewer losing deals · Stronger finance applications

    Smarter choices

    Compare crops, contracts and buyers on likely profit, not just price.

    Fewer losing deals

    See hidden costs, such as long payment terms or high freight, before you commit.

    Stronger finance applications

    Show lenders a clear, data-based view of expected returns.

    Before

    With T57 AI

    On T57, the farmer compares wheat with chickpeas for the coming season. With current fertilizer costs, yield forecasts and a contract farming offer from a verified pulses processor, chickpeas show a higher expected margin and a lower break-even price. The farmer plants half the land with chickpeas under contract and secures input finance against it.

    Why T57 AI

    Validated, verified and accountable

    Transparent assumptionsEvery prediction shows its assumptions and drivers, and members can change them to test their own scenarios.

    AI advises, people decidePredictions support planting, buying and selling decisions. Members decide.

    Is the prediction a guarantee?

    No. It shows the most likely outcome and a range, based on current data. Actual results depend on weather, markets and execution.

    Can I add my own costs?

    Yes. Adding your own costs makes predictions more accurate, and your data stays private.

    T57's document AI solves the retyping, mismatches and delays of trade paperwork, by generating documents from the trade record and checking every document against the others.

    The problem without AI

    Why this is hard without AI

    A single food shipment needs a contract, pro forma and commercial invoices, a packing list, a certificate of origin request, LC documents, an insurance declaration and customs forms. The same data is retyped into each one by different people. A single wrong weight, date or description causes LC discrepancies, customs holds or disputes, and in food, delays mean spoiled goods and lost money.

    How the AI works

    Data in, a small local model, a person decides

    Model typeTemplate generation from structured trade data, document understanding models that read partner documents, and consistency-checking models. A language model drafts clauses and explanations.
    Data inputsThe accepted quote and contract. Verified party details from T57 Passports. Product, packaging and HS code data. LC terms. Shipping, inspection and certificate documents uploaded by partners. Destination document rules.
    OutputReady-to-sign trade documents, a checklist of what each shipment still needs, and a discrepancy report that flags mismatched fields before documents are sent to banks or customs.

    See it in the trade flow: Customs & Documentation Hub

    What it delivers

    Data entered once · Fewer discrepancies · Faster shipments

    Data entered once

    Documents generated from the accepted quote, with no retyping.

    Fewer discrepancies

    Every document checked against the contract, the LC and the others.

    Faster shipments

    Complete, consistent document sets ready before the goods move.

    Checked, not just generatedEvery generated document is checked against the contract and LC, and every check is recorded on the trade record.

    Contracts, pro forma and commercial invoices, packing lists, LC applications and supporting documents, and data for certificates and customs declarations.

    Platform

    The food operating system. One platform, one record.

    The food operating system: one platform that connects every party, service and record in food trade.

    Book a platform demoSee how it works

    What the platform changes

    1. IdentityWithout T57: Checked again by every partyWith T57: Verified once, trusted everywhere
    2. RecordsWithout T57: Dozens of disconnected copiesWith T57: One shared trade record
    3. ServicesWithout T57: Bought separatelyWith T57: Connected inside the trade

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 exists to give food trade the shared infrastructure it has never had: verified identity, one trade record, connected services and AI, running on one secure platform.

    The problem

    Food trade has no shared identity, record or intelligence

    Food is one of the largest traded goods in the world. The global food import bill reached a record of about $2.22 trillion in 2025 (FAO, June 2026). Yet the trade still runs on disconnected systems: each bank, insurer, forwarder, inspector and customs authority keeps its own records, in its own format, about the same trade. Nothing connects them, so trust is rebuilt at every step, and errors and fraud slip through the gaps. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    No shared identity

    Every party verifies every other party from scratch.

    No shared record

    The same trade exists in dozens of disconnected systems and documents.

    No shared intelligence

    Data that could improve pricing, finance and food security stays locked in silos.

    How the platform works

    Trust layer → Trade layer → Services layer → Intelligence and record layers

    1. 01

      Trust layer

      Verifies every member (KYC/KYB, physical checks and compliance screening) and issues the T57 Passport and role labels.

    2. 02

      Trade layer

      Runs RFQs, quotes, contracts, orders and the Trade Desk on one trade record.

    3. 03

      Services layer

      Connects licensed partners for payments, escrow, letters of credit, finance, insurance, logistics, inspection and customs through APIs.

    4. 04

      Intelligence and record layers

      AI models support every step, and key records are anchored on a tamper-evident blockchain ledger.

    Platform components

    8 parts, one platform

    Identity and verification

    KYC, KYB, physical verification and the T57 Passport. For every member, this means verified once and trusted everywhere on T57.

    Trade record

    A single, shared record of every quote, contract, document, milestone and payment. For all parties, this means one version of the truth.

    Trade workflow

    RFQs, quotes, contracts from quotes, orders and contract farming. For buyers and sellers, this means structured, consistent deals.

    Partner integration hub

    API connections to banks, payment institutions, insurers, takaful operators, logistics firms, inspectors and customs systems. For members, this means services inside the trade.

    Intelligence layer

    Small, local AI models for matching, pricing, forecasting, risk, compliance and documents. For members, this means expert support at every step.

    Blockchain layer

    Tamper-evident anchoring of key records, tokenized trade documents and smart-contract milestones. For lenders and regulators, this means records they can trust.

    Security and data protection

    Multi-region cloud infrastructure on Microsoft Azure, designed for data residency, encryption and access control. For members, this means data that is protected and stays where the law requires.

    Open APIs

    Integration with members' ERP, accounting and procurement systems. For larger businesses, this means T57 fits into their existing tools.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    Riyadh food group connects its systems to T57

    A Riyadh food group runs its own ERP for purchasing and finance. It connects the ERP to T57 through APIs, so RFQs, contracts and invoices flow both ways. Its suppliers are verified on T57, its bank receives verified deal files for finance, and its customs broker receives documents before shipments arrive. The group's teams keep using their own systems, while every trade runs on one shared, trusted record.

    Why T57

    We believe that food trade needs shared infrastructure, the way payments and shipping already have it.

    Built for compliance and securityThe platform is designed for data residency in each market, consent-based data sharing and a full audit trail. People review every adverse decision.
    Institutional backingT57 works with the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS) under a 10-year memorandum of understanding.

    T57 is a platform: a members-only verified trade club with the infrastructure to run trades end to end. Members trade directly with each other on it.

    Can T57 connect to my existing systems?

    Yes. T57 offers APIs for ERP, accounting and procurement systems, and connects to partner banks, insurers and logistics providers.

    Where is my data stored?

    On Microsoft Azure cloud infrastructure across regions, designed to meet each market's data-residency requirements.

    Platform · Architecture

    Cloud-native. API-first. Built for regulated trade.

    A cloud-native, API-first architecture built for verified, regulated, cross-border food trade.

    Talk to our integration teamSee how it works

    What the platform changes

    1. IntegrationWithout T57: Custom projects for every partnerWith T57: Standard connectors and APIs
    2. Data lawsWithout T57: A barrier to crossing bordersWith T57: Region-aware storage
    3. ReliabilityWithout T57: Single points of failureWith T57: Modular, monitored services

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's architecture solves the integration problem in food trade, by connecting members, partners and authorities to one trade record through secure, region-aware cloud services and open APIs.

    The problem

    Many systems, many data laws, no common language

    Food trade involves banks, insurers, logistics firms, inspectors, customs authorities and thousands of businesses, each with its own systems and rules, in many countries with their own data laws. Most trade platforms are built as closed marketplaces that cannot connect deeply to these parties, or as single-country systems that cannot cross borders. Neither can carry a trade from end to end. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Many systems, no common language

    Partners and members use different formats for the same data.

    Data laws by country

    Data must often stay in-country, or be shared only on specific terms.

    Scale and reliability

    Trade infrastructure must stay available and consistent across time zones and markets.

    How the architecture works

    Cloud foundation → Core services → Integration layer → Intelligence and ledger

    1. 01

      Cloud foundation

      Cloud-native services on Microsoft Azure across regions, with data stored to meet each market's residency rules.

    2. 02

      Core services

      Identity and verification, trade record, workflow, documents and payments orchestration, each a separate service with its own controls.

    3. 03

      Integration layer

      APIs and connectors for partner banks, insurers, logistics providers, inspectors, customs systems and members' ERPs.

    4. 04

      Intelligence and ledger

      AI services and a blockchain layer that read from and anchor the trade record, under strict access rules.

    Architecture components

    8 parts, one platform

    Region-aware data storage

    Data hosted to meet local residency requirements. For regulated members and partners, this supports compliance.

    Modular services

    Identity, trade, documents, payments orchestration and notifications as separate services. For reliability, this limits the impact of any single failure.

    Event-driven trade record

    Every action is recorded as an event, which builds a complete history. For audit, this means nothing is lost or overwritten.

    Partner connectors

    Standard connectors for banks, payment institutions, insurers and logistics systems. For partners, this means faster onboarding.

    Member APIs

    REST APIs and webhooks for ERP, accounting and procurement integration. For enterprises, this means T57 fits their workflow.

    Standards-based data

    Trade data mapped to recognized standards such as HS codes, Incoterms and electronic trade document formats. For partners, this means interoperability.

    Consent and permissions engine

    Controls who sees what on each trade. For members, this keeps commercial data private.

    Monitoring and resilience

    Continuous monitoring, backups and recovery across regions. For members, this means a platform they can rely on.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    Malaysian bank connects to T57 for trade finance

    A Malaysian bank wants to finance more SME food trades but cannot assess small deals cheaply. It connects to T57 through the partner API. Finance requests arrive as structured, verified deal files that its credit system can read directly. Disbursement and repayment events flow back to the trade record, and escrow repays the bank at settlement. The bank's data stays within its own systems and the residency rules it must follow.

    Why T57

    We believe that trade infrastructure should connect everyone without forcing anyone to replace their systems.

    Designed for regulated partnersData residency, consent-based sharing, permissions and a full audit trail are built into the architecture, not added later.
    Open by designAPIs and standard data formats let banks, logistics firms and authorities connect without custom projects for every trade.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Which cloud does T57 use?

    Microsoft Azure, across regions, designed to meet each market's data-residency requirements.

    Does T57 offer APIs?

    Yes. Members and partners can integrate through REST APIs and webhooks. Documentation is available to approved members and partners.

    Can partners keep their data in their own systems?

    Yes. Partners exchange only the data each trade needs, under agreement and with consent, and keep their own systems of record.

    The problem

    Infrastructure people depend on cannot be built all at once

    Food trade infrastructure cannot be built all at once. Trust has to come first, because finance and data are only valuable when they rest on verified members and records. Many platforms promise everything on day one and deliver little. T57 is built in deliberate stages, with each layer strengthening the next. The key challenges this approach addresses include:

    Trust before scale

    Verification and the trade record must be solid before finance and data can rely on them.

    Partners at their own pace

    Banks, insurers and authorities join and integrate on their own timelines.

    Market by market

    Each market opens when both its supply and demand sides are ready.

    How the platform grows

    Verified trade → Connected finance → Food ecosystem → Expanding markets

    1. 01

      Verified trade

      Membership verification, the T57 Passport and role labels, RFQs and quotes, contracts from quotes, matching, compliance screening, price data, and partner escrow, letters of credit, insurance and logistics.

    2. 02

      Connected finance

      Multi-lender finance requests, blockchain records and smart-contract milestones, forecasting, wallets in any currency, and deeper insurance and takaful.

    3. 03

      Food ecosystem

      Small, local AI models at scale, digital banking and alternative payments, trade data services, paperless pre-clearance with customs authorities, the food security view for governments, contract farming and the agronomy network.

    4. 04

      Expanding markets

      Starting with Saudi Arabia, the UAE, India, Malaysia and Türkiye, then opening further corridors across the OIC, ASEAN, Africa and beyond.

    What each stage brings

    4 ways each stage helps

    For buyers and sellers

    Verified partners and one trade record first, then easier finance, then deeper intelligence and services.

    For lenders and insurers

    Verified deal files first, then structured multi-lender requests and self-liquidating trades, then richer risk data.

    For governments

    Verified supplier data first, then pre-clearance and the food security view.

    For farmers and cooperatives

    Market access first, then contract farming, crop forecasting and agronomy support.

As connected finance arrives, it uses multi-lender requests to fund the harvest. Later, it adopts crop forecasting and contract farming, so it can agree volumes with buyers before the season starts.

    Why T57

    We believe that infrastructure people depend on should be built carefully, one strong layer at a time.

    Transparent directionMembers and partners can see where the platform is heading and plan their own integration.
    Built with partnersEach stage is developed with banks, insurers, logistics firms and authorities, not around them.

    What the platform changes

    TodayWith T57

    T57's intelligence layer solves the problem of AI built on unreliable data, by training small, local models on verified trade records and consented local knowledge, and governing them so people stay in charge.

    The problem

    AI is only as good as its data

    AI is only as good as its data. Most food trade data is incomplete, unverified or locked in private systems, and general-purpose AI models know little about local crops, grades, markets or languages. AI used for decisions about credit, compliance or market access must also be explainable and fair, or it does more harm than good. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Unreliable data

    Unverified listings and scattered records produce unreliable AI.

    One-size-fits-all models

    Global models miss local conditions, products and languages.

    Unaccountable decisions

    Black-box AI cannot be trusted with decisions that affect livelihoods.

    How the intelligence layer works

    Verified data in → Small, local models → Services out → Governance throughout

    1. 01

      Verified data in

      Models learn from verified trade records, public and licensed market data, and farmer knowledge recorded with consent.

    2. 02

      Small, local models

      A family of models for each region, crop and value chain, plus language models with Arabic and local-language knowledge.

    3. 03

      Services out

      Models power matching, pricing, forecasting, risk, compliance, negotiation support, ordering and documents across the platform.

    4. 04

      Governance throughout

      Models are documented, tested and monitored. Outputs carry confidence levels, and people review every adverse decision.

    Components

    7 parts, one platform

    Data foundation

    Verified trade records, market data and consented local knowledge. For model quality, this means reliable inputs.

    Model library

    Small, local models for each region and crop, and shared models for documents and language. For members, this means AI that understands their market.

    AI services

    Matching, price index, forecasting, risk scoring, compliance, negotiation support, ordering and document generation. For every member, this means expert help at each step.

    Explanations and confidence

    Every output shows its reasons and confidence. For members and regulators, this means AI they can question.

    Human review workflow

    Adverse decisions go to trained reviewers, with a stated reason and a route to contest. For members, this means fairness.

    Model monitoring

    Continuous checks for accuracy, drift and bias. For everyone, this means AI that stays reliable over time.

    Privacy controls

    Individual data is never exposed to other members, and institutional views use aggregated, permissioned data. For members, this protects confidentiality.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A forecasting model learns a new crop in Malaysia

    T57 adds durian to its Malaysian models as exports grow. Verified trades on the platform, public price data and growers' recorded observations about flowering and weather, shared with consent, train a small local forecasting model. It is tested against past seasons before release, each forecast shows its confidence, and growers and buyers use it to plan harvests and shipments.

    Why T57

    We believe that AI in food trade must be useful, local and accountable.

    Responsible AI by designNo business is denied market access by an automated decision alone. Every adverse decision is reviewed by a person, with a stated reason and a route to contest it.
    Governance built around recognized frameworksT57's AI governance follows the risk-based principles of the EU AI Act and the ISO/IEC 42001 AI management standard.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Does T57 use my data to train AI?

    T57 uses verified trade data in anonymized, aggregated form to improve its models. Your individual data is never shown to other members, and farmer knowledge is used only with consent.

    Why not just use a large general AI model?

    Large models are useful for language and documents, and T57 uses them where they fit. For crops, markets and local conditions, small models trained on local data are more accurate, cheaper to run and easier to test and explain.

    Can I challenge an AI decision?

    Yes. Every adverse decision comes with a reason and a route to contest it, and a person reviews it.

    Platform · Blockchain Layer

    Records no one can quietly change. Payments that follow proof.

    Tamper-evident records, tokenized documents and milestone payments that every party can trust.

    See the blockchain layer in a demoSee how it works

    What the platform changes

    1. DocumentsWithout T57: Altered after the factWith T57: Any change can be detected
    2. InvoicesWithout T57: Financed twiceWith T57: One token, one owner
    3. PaymentsWithout T57: Disputed milestonesWith T57: Released on recorded proof

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's blockchain layer solves the problem of trade records that can be altered, duplicated or disputed, by anchoring key records on a ledger and automating payments when agreed milestones are recorded.

    The problem

    Documents that can be altered, pledged twice and disputed

    Trade fraud often comes down to documents: an invoice financed twice, a warehouse receipt for goods that do not exist, a certificate changed after inspection. Disputes drag on because nobody can prove which version of a document is real, or when a milestone happened. Paper and PDFs make this easy to exploit and hard to prevent. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Altered documents

    Documents can be changed after the fact without detection.

    Double financing

    The same invoice or receipt can be pledged with several lenders.

    Slow, disputed payments

    Payment depends on parties agreeing that milestones were met.

    How the blockchain layer works

    Record → Anchor → Tokenize → Automate

    1. 01

      Record

      Documents and milestones are stored securely on the T57 trade record.

    2. 02

      Anchor

      A digital fingerprint of each key record is written to a blockchain ledger. Any later change to the document can be detected.

    3. 03

      Tokenize

      Eligible trade documents, such as invoices and warehouse receipts, can be issued as unique tokens linked to their owner and trade.

    4. 04

      Automate

      Smart contracts check recorded milestones, such as an inspection pass or delivery confirmation, and instruct licensed partners to release payments.

    Components

    7 parts, one platform

    Record anchoring

    Fingerprints of key records written to the ledger. For auditors and lenders, this proves documents have not changed.

    Privacy by design

    Only fingerprints go on the ledger, never document contents. For members, this protects commercial data.

    Tokenized trade documents

    Unique digital tokens for invoices, warehouse receipts and bills of lading. For lenders, this prevents double financing.

    Smart-contract milestones

    Coded release rules linked to escrow and finance. For sellers, this means faster, automatic payment.

    Permissioned access

    Only authorized parties can see each trade's records. For regulated partners, this supports compliance.

    Electronic trade document readiness

    Designed to support electronic trade documents where laws such as the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records apply. For exporters, this prepares for paperless trade.

    Verification tools

    Partners and authorities can check a document's fingerprint against the ledger. For customs and banks, this means fast authenticity checks.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    Dubai lender avoids a double-financed invoice

    A Dubai finance company receives a request to fund an invoice from a food trader. Because the invoice was issued as a token on T57, the lender can see that it is unique, linked to a verified delivery and not pledged elsewhere. It funds the invoice. When the buyer confirms delivery, a smart-contract milestone instructs the escrow partner to repay the lender automatically.

    Why T57

    We believe that trust in trade should rest on records anyone authorized can check.

    Built for regulated financePayments are always made by licensed partners. Smart contracts only instruct them when agreed conditions are met. T57 does not hold client funds or digital assets.
    Privacy and permissions firstCommercial data stays off the public ledger, and every party sees only what it is allowed to see.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Is my trade data public on the blockchain?

    No. Only digital fingerprints of key records are anchored. Document contents stay in secure storage, visible only to authorized parties.

    Do I need cryptocurrency to use the blockchain layer?

    No. The blockchain layer works in the background. Members pay and get paid in normal currencies through licensed partners, unless they choose alternative payments where lawful.

    What happens if a milestone is disputed?

    The smart contract pauses release, and the dispute is handled under the contract and the partner's rules.

    T57's security architecture exists to protect the trade data, identities and documents that members trust to the platform, with layered controls, data residency by region and a full audit trail.

    The problem

    Food trade runs on sensitive information

    Food trade runs on sensitive information: prices, buyers, bank details, identity documents and contracts. A single breach can expose a business to fraud or competitors, and many countries now require certain data to stay within their borders. Members and regulated partners need to know exactly how their data is protected and who can see it. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Sensitive data at risk

    Trade, identity and payment details are valuable targets for fraud.

    Data residency rules

    Many founding markets require local storage or control of certain data.

    Unclear access

    Members cannot always see who accessed their information, and when.

    How T57 protects your data

    Verified identity → Least-privilege access → Protected data → Monitored and recorded

    1. 01

      Verified identity

      Every member is verified before trading, and every user signs in with strong, multi-factor authentication.

    2. 02

      Least-privilege access

      Role-based permissions mean each person and partner sees only what their role and trade require.

    3. 03

      Protected data

      Data is encrypted in transit and at rest, and hosted on Microsoft Azure in multiple regions built for data residency.

    4. 04

      Monitored and recorded

      Activity is logged, monitored for unusual behavior and recorded in an audit trail, with key records anchored on a ledger.

    Components

    9 parts, one platform

    Identity verification

    KYC and KYB checks through licensed partners. For members, this means every counterparty is real.

    Multi-factor authentication

    Strong sign-in for every user. For members, this stops stolen passwords being enough.

    Role-based access control

    Permissions by role, company and trade. For businesses, this keeps staff and partner access tight.

    Encryption

    Data encrypted in transit and at rest. For members, this protects information if systems are compromised.

    Regional hosting and data residency

    Multi-region Azure hosting, with data kept in-region where rules require it. For members and regulators, this supports local data laws.

    Consent management

    Members control how their data is shared and used. For farmers and businesses, this means data used only with permission.

    Audit trail

    A record of who did what, and when. For members and auditors, this means full accountability.

    Threat monitoring and response

    Continuous monitoring with defined incident response. For everyone, this means issues are found and handled fast.

    Secure development

    Security reviews and testing built into how T57 is built. For members, this reduces risk from the start.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Riyadh importer controls who sees its supplier data

    A Riyadh food importer adds its finance manager, buyers and an outside customs broker to T57. Each gets a role: buyers see orders and suppliers, the finance manager sees payments, and the customs broker sees only the documents for the shipments assigned to them. The importer's data is hosted in-region, and its admin can review the audit trail at any time.

    Why T57

    We believe that a trusted trade network must start with trusted data handling.

    Security by designIdentity, access control, encryption and audit are part of the platform architecture, not add-ons.
    Built for data residencyMulti-region hosting lets T57 meet local data rules across its founding markets.
    Transparent to membersMembers can see who accessed their data and control how it is shared.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Where is my data stored?

    T57 is hosted on Microsoft Azure in multiple regions. Where local rules require it, data is stored in-region.

    Can other members see my prices or suppliers?

    No. Your commercial data is visible only to you and the parties in your trades, according to the permissions you set.

    What happens if there is a security incident?

    T57 follows a defined incident response process, and affected members and authorities are notified as the law requires.
