    Trust & Compliance

    Know who you trade with. Prove what happened.

    Trade with verified businesses, on one record, under clear rules.

    Get verified and join T57See how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. CounterpartiesWithout T57: Unknown, uncheckedWith T57: Verified and role-labelled
    2. RecordsWithout T57: Paper and scattered filesWith T57: One record with an audit trail
    3. When it goes wrongWithout T57: No clear processWith T57: Escrow paused, dispute on the record

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 exists to make trust the starting point of food trade. Every member is verified, every trade is recorded, and regulated services come only through licensed partners.

    The problem

    Food trade still runs on hope that the other side is who they say they are.

    Buyers often cannot tell a producer from a reseller. Documents are forged, invoices are financed twice and contracts go unenforced across borders. Banks feel this too: weak data on smaller firms is one reason the Asian Development Bank reports that 41% of SME trade finance applications were rejected in 2025. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Unknown counterparties

    Businesses cannot easily confirm who they are trading with, or whether they own what they sell.

    Unreliable records

    Paper and scattered files make it hard to prove what was agreed and what happened.

    Unclear accountability

    When a trade goes wrong, there is often no clear process or record to resolve it.

    How T57 builds trust

    Verify → Label → Record → Assure

    1. 01

      Verify

      Every buyer and seller passes KYC and KYB checks, sanctions screening and, where they claim to produce, physical verification.

    2. 02

      Label

      Each member is labelled as owner-producer, processor, trader or intermediary, so you always know who you deal with.

    3. 03

      Record

      Quotes, contracts, documents and milestones sit on one shared trade record, with an audit trail and tamper-evident anchoring.

    4. 04

      Assure

      Escrow, letters of credit and insurance come through licensed partners, and a structured dispute process applies if a party does not perform.

    What the trust layer includes

    The trust layer, part by part

    Verification processA five-stage check before anyone can trade. For buyers, this means every seller is real.
    KYB and KYCChecks on companies, owners and directors. For lenders, this means known customers.
    T57 PassportA reusable verified profile, shared with consent. For members, this means verifying once and trading widely.
    Membership scoring and trust ratingA rating built from verified trade behavior. For counterparties, this means evidence, not reputation.
    Audit trailA record of every action on every trade. For auditors and regulators, this means full traceability.
    Document managementSecure, versioned trade documents with authenticity checks. For exporters, this means faster clearance and fewer disputes.
    Security and privacyEncryption, access control and consent. For members, this means confidential data stays confidential.
    Data protectionCompliance with each founding market's data law. For members and regulators, this means lawful data use.
    Dispute resolutionA clear, recorded process when something goes wrong. For both sides, this means fair and faster outcomes.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Kuala Lumpur importer checks a new Indian supplier in minutes

    A Malaysian rice importer finds a new basmati supplier on T57. The supplier's Passport shows it is a verified owner-producer, its mill was visited by T57's India team, its export licence is current, and it has a record of completed trades on the platform. The importer agrees terms, pays into escrow through a licensed partner and tracks every document on one record.

    Why T57

    We believe that trust in food trade should be earned, checked and visible, not assumed.

    Verified people, not anonymous listingsT57 is a members-only trade club, not an open marketplace. Verification is renewed, and members are suspended for misrepresentation.
    Built to meet the rules where we tradeT57 is designed around the data protection and compliance laws of its founding markets, and leaves payments, escrow, letters of credit and lending to licensed partners. T57 does not hold client funds.
    Institutional backingT57 works with institutions across its founding markets, including a 10-year MoU with the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS).

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Is T57 an open marketplace?

    No. T57 is a members-only trade club. Every buyer and seller is verified before trading, and verification is renewed.

    Does T57 hold my money?

    No. Payments, escrow and letters of credit are handled by licensed partners. T57 organizes the trade and records each step.

    How do I know who I am trading with?

    Every member has a verified T57 Passport that shows their role, checks passed and trade history, shared with consent.

    What happens if a trade goes wrong?

    T57 provides a structured dispute process based on the shared trade record, and escrow can pause release while a dispute is resolved.

    Trust & Compliance · Verification

    Verified on the ground, not just on screen.

    Know exactly who you are trading with, before you trade.

    Start your verificationSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. RoleWithout T57: Producer or middleman?With T57: Labelled owner-producer to intermediary
    2. DocumentsWithout T57: Forged or expiredWith T57: Checked for authenticity
    3. ProducersWithout T57: ClaimedWith T57: Site visit by a local team

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's verification process solves the problem of fake, misrepresented and unknown counterparties, by checking every member's identity, ownership, licences and role before they can trade.

    The problem

    On open marketplaces, anyone can list a product.

    A reseller can pose as a farm, a shell company can pose as an exporter, and a sanctioned party can hide behind a new name. Checking a new partner yourself takes weeks of calls, documents and site visits that most businesses cannot afford. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Misrepresented roles

    Buyers cannot tell a producer from a middleman.

    Fake or unlicensed businesses

    Forged documents and expired licences are hard to spot.

    Hidden risk

    Sanctioned or high-risk parties are difficult to screen without specialist tools.

    How verification works

    Apply → KYC and KYB → Physical verification → Role label and Passport

    1. 01

      Apply

      The business submits company documents, owners, licences, bank details and the role it claims.

    2. 02

      KYC and KYB

      T57 checks owners and directors, company registration, beneficial ownership, sanctions and watchlists, and document authenticity. AI triages each file, and an analyst reviews it.

    3. 03

      Physical verification

      T57's country team visits farms, factories and warehouses, and checks proof of ownership, such as a land title, lease or production licence, for anyone who claims to produce.

    4. 04

      Role label and Passport

      The member is labelled owner-producer, processor, trader or intermediary, and receives a verified T57 Passport.

    Verification does not stop there. Expiry reminders, periodic re-verification and continuous screening keep every Passport current.

    Features

    What is included

    Document checksAuthenticity checks on registration papers, licences and IDs. For buyers, this filters out forged paperwork.
    Registry checksRegistration, directors and owners confirmed against official sources where available. For lenders, this confirms the company is real.
    Sanctions and watchlist screeningEvery member and trade screened. For everyone, this keeps the network clean.
    Physical verificationSite visits by local country teams. For buyers, this proves the producer exists.
    Role labellingClear labels for owner-producer, processor, trader and intermediary. For buyers, this means knowing whether you deal with the source.
    Human reviewAnalysts make the final decision, with AI as an aid. For applicants, this means fair treatment and a stated reason if declined.
    Ongoing checksRe-verification, reminders and suspension for misconduct. For members, this keeps trust current.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Jeddah buyer confirms a Turkish hazelnut grower owns its orchards

    A Saudi distributor wants to buy hazelnuts direct from the source. On T57, it filters for owner-producers in Türkiye and finds a grower whose Passport shows a site visit by T57's Türkiye team and a verified land title. The distributor buys direct, knowing it is not paying a middleman's margin.

    Why T57

    We believe that verification must be done on the ground, not only on screen.

    Local teams in every founding marketT57 has onboarding and verification staff in each country, because some checks cannot be done from a distance.
    AI advises, people decideAI speeds up document and risk checks, but an analyst makes every decision, and any applicant who is declined is told why and can ask for a review.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    How long does verification take?

    It depends on the business and whether a site visit is needed. T57 tells you what is outstanding at each stage.

    Why does T57 visit my farm or factory?

    To confirm that businesses claiming to produce really do. This is what lets buyers trust the owner-producer label.

    Do I need to verify again for each trade?

    No. Your T57 Passport is reusable. It is renewed periodically, and you update it when your details change.

    What if my application is declined?

    You receive a stated reason and can ask for a review by a person.

    Trust & Compliance · KYB

    The real business behind every trade.

    Verify the business behind every trade.

    Start business verificationSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. CompanyWithout T57: A name and a websiteWith T57: Confirmed against registries
    2. OwnersWithout T57: HiddenWith T57: Identified and screened
    3. LicencesWithout T57: Lapsed unnoticedWith T57: Tracked with expiry reminders

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's Know Your Business (KYB) checks confirm that every member company is real, properly registered, licensed and owned by the people it names.

    The problem

    A company name and a website prove very little.

    Shell companies, borrowed licences and hidden owners are common routes to fraud and sanctions breaches in cross-border trade. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Shell and fake companies

    Businesses that exist only on paper.

    Hidden ownership

    Owners who are not disclosed, or who are sanctioned.

    Expired licences

    Export, food-safety or trading licences that have lapsed.

    How KYB works

    Submit → Check → Screen → Approve and monitor

    1. 01

      Submit

      The business uploads registration documents, licences, ownership details and bank information.

    2. 02

      Check

      T57 confirms registration, directors and beneficial owners against official registries where available, and checks document authenticity.

    3. 03

      Screen

      The company and its owners are screened against sanctions and watchlists.

    4. 04

      Approve and monitor

      An analyst approves the file, and licences are tracked with expiry reminders and periodic re-checks.

    Features

    What is included

    Registry confirmationChecks against official business registries where available. For buyers, this proves the company exists.
    Beneficial ownershipThe real owners identified and screened. For lenders and partners, this supports their compliance duties.
    Licence trackingLicences and certifications recorded on the Passport with expiry reminders. For importers, this means current paperwork.
    Bank detail verificationAccount details confirmed. For sellers and buyers, this reduces payment-redirect fraud.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    An Abu Dhabi trader passes KYB once and uses it everywhere

    A UAE trading company completes KYB on T57. Its verified Passport, shared with consent, lets it start trading with suppliers in India and Malaysia, and apply for trade finance through a partner bank, without resubmitting the same company documents each time.

    Why T57

    Why members and partners trust it

    Verify once, trade widelyThe T57 Passport is reusable, so members do not repeat the same checks for every partner.
    Built for regulated partnersKYB results help licensed partners meet their own customer due diligence, with the member's consent.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    What documents do I need for KYB?

    Company registration, licences, details of directors and owners, and bank information. The exact list depends on your country and role.

    Who sees my KYB documents?

    T57's verification team. Others see only your verified Passport, and only what you choose to share.

    How often is KYB renewed?

    Periodically, and whenever key details such as ownership or licences change.

    Can a cooperative pass KYB on behalf of its farmers?

    Yes. A cooperative or producer organization is verified as a business, and its member producers are onboarded through it.

    Trust & Compliance · KYC

    Every signature, a verified person.

    Verify the people who own and act for every member.

    Start verificationSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. SignersWithout T57: UnknownWith T57: Identity checked
    2. ScreeningWithout T57: SkippedWith T57: Sanctions and watchlists
    3. PrivacyWithout T57: Documents passed aroundWith T57: Seen only by the verification team

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's Know Your Customer (KYC) checks confirm the identity of every owner, director and authorized user, so you always know who is behind a trade.

    The problem

    Why trust is hard in food trade

    Businesses are run by people, and fraud usually starts with a false identity: a fake director, a stolen ID, or an unauthorized person signing a contract. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    False identities

    Stolen or forged identity documents.

    Unauthorized signers

    People acting for a company without authority.

    Sanctioned individuals

    People who should not be trading at all.

    How KYC works

    Identify → Confirm → Screen → Authorize

    1. 01

      Identify

      Owners, directors and users submit identity documents.

    2. 02

      Confirm

      T57 checks document authenticity and confirms that the person matches the document.

    3. 03

      Screen

      Each person is screened against sanctions and watchlists.

    4. 04

      Authorize

      Each user is linked to the company with a defined role and signing authority.

    Features

    What is included

    Identity document checksAuthenticity checks on IDs and passports. For members, this stops impostors.
    Liveness and match checksConfirmation that the person is real and matches the ID. For lenders, this means trusted signers.
    ScreeningSanctions and watchlist checks for every person. For partners, this supports compliance.
    Authority mappingWho can view, quote, sign or approve payments. For businesses, this controls who acts in their name.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Pune processor adds a new export manager

    An Indian spice processor hires a new export manager. Before the manager can sign contracts on T57, they complete KYC and are given authority to quote and sign up to a set value, while payments still need the finance director's approval.

    Why T57

    Why members and partners trust it

    Every signature traced to a verified personContracts and approvals on T57 are linked to verified individuals, recorded in the audit trail.
    Privacy respectedIdentity documents are used only for verification and are protected under each market's data law.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Who needs to complete KYC?

    Owners, directors and anyone who will act for the company on T57.

    Is my ID shared with other members?

    No. Other members see that you are verified, not your documents.

    What if I leave the company?

    The company removes your access, and your past actions stay in the audit trail.

    Can I use one identity for several companies?

    Yes. Each company link is verified separately, with its own role and authority.

    Trust & Compliance · Trust Rating

    Trust built on evidence, not reputation.

    Let your track record speak for your business.

    Build your trust rating on T57See how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. ReputationWithout T57: Word of mouthWith T57: Verified trade behaviour
    2. FeedbackWithout T57: Anyone can postWith T57: Tied to completed trades
    3. FairnessWithout T57: Opaque scoresWith T57: Contestable, reviewed by people

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's trust rating solves the problem of judging new partners on reputation alone, by building a rating from verified checks and real trade behavior on the platform.

    The problem

    In food trade, reputation travels by word of mouth.

    Good small producers struggle to prove they are reliable, and buyers and lenders fall back on size and familiarity. Reviews on open platforms are easy to fake. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    No proof of reliability

    Good performers have no way to show their record.

    Fake reviews

    Ratings that anyone can write are easy to game.

    Opaque scores

    Scores that cannot be explained cannot be trusted or improved.

    How the trust rating works

    Verified start → Trade behavior → Counterparty feedback → Explained results

    1. 01

      Verified start

      Each member's rating begins with their verification level and role.

    2. 02

      Trade behavior

      Completed trades, on-time delivery, document accuracy and payment performance, all taken from the trade record, build the rating.

    3. 03

      Counterparty feedback

      Only parties to a completed trade can rate each other.

    4. 04

      Explained results

      Members see what drives their rating and how to improve it.

    Features

    What is included

    Record-based scoringBuilt from verified trade events, not self-reported claims. For buyers, this means evidence you can rely on.
    Verified feedback onlyRatings tied to completed trades. For members, this prevents fake reviews.
    ExplainabilityClear factors behind every rating. For members, this means knowing how to improve.
    Fair reviewAny rating change that limits access is reviewed by a person, with a route to contest. For members, this means fairness.
    Shared with consentMembers choose who sees their rating, including lenders. For smaller businesses, this turns good performance into access to finance.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Johor durian grower wins a supermarket contract

    A small Malaysian grower has completed 20 trades on T57 with on-time delivery and clean documents. A supermarket chain in the UAE, looking for new suppliers, shortlists the grower on the strength of that record and starts with a trial order.

    Why T57

    Why members and partners trust it

    Evidence, not reputationThe rating comes from what happened on verified trades.
    AI advises, people decideAI helps calculate the rating, but no business loses access because of a score alone.
    Not a credit scoreThe trust rating reflects trade behavior on T57. Credit reports, where used, come from licensed credit bureaus.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    What affects my trust rating?

    Your verification, completed trades, on-time delivery, document accuracy, payment performance and feedback from your trading partners.

    Can I see my own rating?

    Yes, with the main factors behind it.

    Can I dispute a rating?

    Yes. You can contest any rating or feedback, and a person reviews it.

    Do new members start at zero?

    New members start with a rating based on their verification, which grows as they trade.

    Trust & Compliance · Audit & Records

    Who did what, and when. On every trade.

    See who did what, and when, on every trade.

    See the audit trail in a demoSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. HistoryWithout T57: Scattered across emailWith T57: One complete record
    2. ActionsWithout T57: UnattributedWith T57: Linked to a verified person
    3. ChangesWithout T57: SilentWith T57: Tamper-evident

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's audit trail solves the problem of trades that cannot be reconstructed, by recording every action on one trade record from first quote to final settlement.

    The problem

    Why trust is hard in food trade

    When a shipment is rejected, a payment is late or a regulator asks questions, businesses often cannot say who approved what, or which version of a document was used. Emails, chat messages and spreadsheets leave gaps, and gaps lead to disputes, fines and lost finance. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Missing history

    Decisions and changes are scattered across inboxes and phones.

    Version confusion

    Nobody can prove which contract or certificate was final.

    Hard audits

    Auditors, lenders and regulators need evidence that takes weeks to collect.

    How the audit trail works

    Capture → Attribute → Protect → Share

    1. 01

      Capture

      Every action on a trade, such as a quote, edit, approval, signature, document upload or milestone, is recorded automatically.

    2. 02

      Attribute

      Each entry is linked to a verified person, their company and their role, with a timestamp.

    3. 03

      Protect

      Entries cannot be edited or deleted, and fingerprints of key records are anchored on a blockchain ledger, so any change can be detected.

    4. 04

      Share

      Members export the history for an auditor, lender or regulator, with consent.

    Features

    What is included

    Complete trade historyFrom quote to settlement on one record. For managers, this means one place to check.
    Verified attributionEvery action linked to a KYC-verified user. For compliance teams, this means clear accountability.
    Tamper evidenceLedger anchoring of key records. For lenders and auditors, this means proof records have not changed.
    Document versionsEvery version kept, with who changed what. For both sides, this ends version disputes.
    AI decision recordsAI recommendations and the human decisions taken on them are logged. For regulators, this shows people stay in charge.
    Exportable reportsAudit packs for lenders, insurers and authorities. For finance teams, this saves weeks of work.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Chennai exporter answers an insurer's claim review in a day

    A shipment of frozen shrimp from India arrives in Dubai with a temperature complaint. The insurer asks for evidence. The exporter exports the trade's audit trail from T57, showing the inspection report, the temperature logs uploaded at loading, the bill of lading and the buyer's acceptance, each time-stamped and attributed. The claim review moves forward the same day.

    Why T57

    We believe that a trade record is only useful if every party can trust it.

    One record for everyoneBuyer, seller and licensed partners work from the same record, so there is one version of the truth.
    Built for auditThe audit trail is designed for the evidence that lenders, insurers and regulators ask for.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Can anyone edit the audit trail?

    No. Entries cannot be changed or deleted. Corrections are added as new entries.

    Who can see my trade's audit trail?

    The parties to the trade, and anyone they choose to share it with, such as a lender or auditor.

    How long are records kept?

    For the period required by law in each market.

    Are AI decisions recorded?

    Yes. AI recommendations and the human decisions made on them are logged.

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's document management system solves the problem of missing, wrong and forged trade documents, by creating, checking, storing and sharing them on the trade record.

    The problem

    Why trust is hard in food trade

    A single food shipment can need a commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, phytosanitary or health certificate, halal certificate, inspection report and bill of lading. One wrong field or expired certificate can hold cargo at the border, where perishable food loses value every day. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Errors and omissions

    Documents that do not match each other or the destination's rules.

    Forged or expired documents

    Certificates that are fake or out of date.

    Scattered files

    Documents spread across email, couriers and shared drives.

    How document management works

    Create → Collect → Check → Share and verify

    1. 01

      Create

      T57 generates documents such as invoices and packing lists from the agreed contract, so data is entered once.

    2. 02

      Collect

      Partners such as inspectors, insurers and forwarders upload their documents straight to the trade record.

    3. 03

      Check

      AI checks documents against each other and against the destination's requirements, and flags gaps for a person to review.

    4. 04

      Share and verify

      Authorized parties access documents securely, and anyone authorized can check a document's fingerprint against the ledger.

    Features

    What is included

    Document generationInvoices, packing lists and more, filled from the contract. For exporters, this cuts errors and time.
    Requirement checklistsThe documents each destination requires, by product. For new exporters, this means fewer surprises at the border.
    AI consistency checksMismatches between documents flagged before shipping. For traders, this means fewer rejections.
    Expiry trackingAlerts before certificates and licences lapse. For producers, this keeps paperwork current.
    Version controlEvery version kept, with a clear final copy. For both sides, this ends confusion.
    Secure sharingRole-based access for each party. For banks and customs brokers, this means the right documents, fast.
    Authenticity checksFingerprints anchored on a ledger, and tokenized documents for eligible records. For lenders, this prevents double financing.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Bursa cherry exporter clears its first shipment to Riyadh

    A Türkiye cherry exporter is shipping to Saudi Arabia for the first time. T57 lists the documents needed for fresh cherries to the Kingdom, generates the invoice and packing list from the contract, and flags that the phytosanitary certificate shows a different weight from the packing list. The exporter fixes it before loading, and the shipment clears without delay.

    Why T57

    We believe that paperwork should move as fast as food needs to.

    One record, one source of dataDocuments are created from the agreed contract, so the same data flows through every document.
    Ready for paperless tradeT57 is designed to support electronic trade documents where the law allows, such as under the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Which documents can T57 generate?

    Commercial documents such as invoices, packing lists and contract-based forms. Official certificates are issued by the relevant authority or partner and uploaded to the record.

    Does T57 check my documents?

    AI checks for gaps and mismatches and flags them. Your team and your partners make the final decisions.

    Who can see my documents?

    Only the parties you authorize for each trade.

    Are original paper documents still needed?

    In some markets and for some documents, yes. T57 shows where paper originals are still required.

    Trust & Compliance · Security & Privacy

    Your data stays yours. You control who sees it.

    Your trade data stays yours, protected and private.

    Read our Data Protection approachSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. AccessWithout T57: Anyone with a passwordWith T57: Multi-factor sign-in and roles
    2. VisibilityWithout T57: UnknownWith T57: See who accessed what
    3. SharingWithout T57: AssumedWith T57: Only with your consent

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 exists to give food businesses a place to trade where their prices, partners and documents are protected, and where they decide who sees what.

    The problem

    Food businesses guard their buyers, suppliers and margins closely.

    Sharing them on a platform feels risky, and many digital tools give little control over who sees data or how it is used. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Fear of exposure

    Prices and partners leaking to competitors.

    Loss of control

    Not knowing who has seen or used your data.

    Account takeover

    Stolen passwords used to redirect payments or sign deals.

    How T57 protects you

    Secure access → Your rules → Protected storage → Full visibility

    1. 01

      Secure access

      Every user is verified and signs in with multi-factor authentication.

    2. 02

      Your rules

      You decide which staff, partners and counterparties see each piece of information.

    3. 03

      Protected storage

      Data is encrypted and hosted in-region where local rules require it.

    4. 04

      Full visibility

      You can see who accessed your data, and when, in your audit trail.

    Features

    What is included

    Multi-factor sign-inFor every user. For members, this stops stolen passwords being enough.
    Role-based permissionsSet by company, role and trade. For business owners, this keeps control in your hands.
    Consent controlsYour Passport, trade history and rating are shared only when you choose. For members, this means privacy by default.
    Confidential pricingYour prices are visible only to the parties you quote. For sellers, this protects margins.
    Anonymized insightsMarket data and AI use aggregated, anonymized data, never your individual records. For members, this means insight without exposure.
    Access historyA record of who viewed or changed your data. For members, this means transparency.
    Payment safeguardsBank details verified and changes confirmed. For sellers, this reduces payment-redirect fraud.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Dubai trader shares only what each partner needs

    A UAE trading house shares its full Passport with a partner bank for finance, shares only its verification status and rating with a new supplier in India, and keeps its buying prices private from everyone except the sellers it quotes. Its admin reviews the access history each month.

    Why T57

    We believe that privacy is a condition of trust, not a trade-off.

    Privacy by defaultNothing is shared without your consent, beyond what the law and your trades require.
    Security by designIdentity, access control, encryption and audit are built into the platform. See our Security Architecture for the technical detail.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Does T57 sell my data?

    No. T57 does not sell members' individual data. Market insights use aggregated, anonymized data.

    Can T57 staff see my data?

    Only staff who need it for verification, support or compliance, under strict access controls, and access is logged.

    Can I delete my data?

    You can ask for deletion, subject to records the law requires T57 or its partners to keep.

    How do I report a security concern?

    Contact our security team at hello@t57.ai.

    TodayWith T57

    T57 is built to comply with the data protection laws of each of its founding markets, so members and partners can share data with confidence.

    The problem

    Cross-border trade means data crosses borders too.

    Each founding market has its own data protection law, with its own rules on consent, storage and transfer. Businesses need a platform that respects all of them. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Different laws in every market

    Rules on consent, residency and transfers vary.

    Cross-border transfers

    Data must move between markets lawfully.

    Individual rights

    People have rights to access, correct and delete their data.

    How T57 protects data

    Lawful basis → Local rules → Controlled transfers → Rights respected

    1. 01

      Lawful basis

      T57 collects only the data needed for verification, trading and compliance, with consent where required.

    2. 02

      Local rules

      Data handling follows each market's law, with data kept in-region where required.

    3. 03

      Controlled transfers

      Data moves across borders only as the law allows and as the trade requires.

    4. 04

      Rights respected

      Members can access, correct and request deletion of their data, subject to legal retention.

    Laws T57 is built to meet

    Built to meet the law in all five founding markets

    Saudi ArabiaPersonal Data Protection Law (PDPL).
    United Arab EmiratesFederal Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL).
    IndiaDigital Personal Data Protection Act 2023.
    MalaysiaPersonal Data Protection Act 2010.
    TürkiyeLaw No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data.

    T57 is obtaining legal opinions in all five markets before full launch.

Their personal data stays protected under Malaysia's PDPA, and buyers in the Gulf see only the cooperative's verified Passport and product details.

    Why T57

    Consent firstVerification data and farmer knowledge are used only with consent.
    Built for regional data rulesMulti-region hosting supports data residency in each founding market.

    Trust & Compliance · Trade Assurance

    Disputes settled on the facts, not on who shouts loudest.

    Resolve trade disputes on the facts, quickly and fairly.

    Trade with protection on T57See how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. EvidenceWithout T57: Each side's own versionWith T57: One shared record
    2. MoneyWithout T57: Already goneWith T57: Escrow paused until there is an outcome
    3. TimeWithout T57: Months of argumentWith T57: A clear, recorded process

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's dispute process solves the problem of costly, drawn-out trade disputes, by resolving them from the shared trade record, with escrow paused until there is an outcome.

    The problem

    Why trust is hard in food trade

    When a cross-border food trade goes wrong, the goods are often perishable, the parties are in different countries, and the evidence is scattered. Court action is slow and expensive, so small businesses often just take the loss. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    No shared evidence

    Each side holds different documents and messages.

    Money at risk

    Payments are made or lost before the facts are clear.

    Slow, costly remedies

    Cross-border legal action is out of reach for most.

    How dispute resolution works

    Raise → Pause → Review → Resolve

    1. 01

      Raise

      Either party opens a dispute on the trade record, stating the issue, such as quality, quantity, delay or documents.

    2. 02

      Pause

      Where the trade uses escrow, the licensed escrow partner holds the disputed amount, and partial release is possible for any undisputed part.

    3. 03

      Review

      Both sides add evidence, such as inspection reports, photos and logs, to the record. T57 helps the parties reach an agreement based on the agreed terms.

    4. 04

      Resolve

      The parties settle, or the dispute moves to the route set in their contract. The outcome is recorded, and escrow is released accordingly.

    Features

    What is included

    Dispute on the recordEvery claim and response in one place. For both sides, this means a clear, shared view.
    Evidence from the recordContracts, documents and milestones already in place. For both sides, this saves time.
    Escrow pause and partial releaseThrough licensed partners. For sellers and buyers, this protects money during a dispute.
    Independent inspectionInspection partners can be called to assess goods. For buyers, this means objective evidence.
    Recorded outcomesOutcomes feed into each member's trust rating. For the network, this rewards fair dealing.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Riyadh importer and a Gujarat exporter settle a quality claim

    A Saudi importer reports that part of a groundnut shipment is below the agreed grade. The disputed amount stays in escrow while the rest is released to the exporter. A partner inspector tests samples and confirms that 8% of the bags are below grade. The parties agree a price adjustment on the record, and escrow releases the balance.

    Why T57

    Why members and partners trust it

    Facts firstDisputes are resolved from the shared trade record, not from competing stories.
    Fair to both sidesThe process is clear, recorded and the same for every member, and misconduct can lead to suspension.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    What disputes does T57 cover?

    Disputes over trades made on T57, such as quality, quantity, delivery, documents and payment.

    Does T57 decide who is right?

    T57 helps the parties reach an agreement based on the record and their contract. Where they cannot agree, the dispute follows the route set in the contract.

    What happens to my money during a dispute?

    If the trade uses escrow, the disputed amount is held by the licensed escrow partner until the dispute is resolved.

    Does a dispute affect my trust rating?

    The outcome is recorded. A fair resolution does not count against either side, and you can contest any rating effect.

    What you get with T57

    1. MarketsWithout T57: Different rules everywhereWith T57: One record across five markets
    2. TrustWithout T57: Hard across bordersWith T57: Verified locally, trusted everywhere
    3. TeamsWithout T57: Global, far awayWith T57: Local teams in each market

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 connects verified food producers, traders and buyers in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, India, Malaysia and Türkiye, on one trade record that works within each country and across their borders.

    The challenge

    The world spent an estimated $2.22 trillion on food imports in 2025 (FAO).

    Much of that trade flows between the regions T57 serves: Gulf economies that import most of their food, and producing nations in South Asia, Southeast Asia and Türkiye that want to sell more of it, directly. Yet each market has its own rules, documents, languages and ways of doing business, and trust across borders is hard to build. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Fragmented markets

    Each country has different rules, documents and platforms.

    Trust across borders

    Buyers and sellers in different countries cannot easily verify each other.

    Local needs

    Global platforms rarely fit local languages, crops, regulations and payment habits.

    How T57 works across markets

    1. 01

      Local verification

      Country teams verify members in each market, on the ground.

    2. 02

      Domestic wholesale

      Producers and manufacturers sell to supermarkets, hotels, restaurants, caterers and institutions in their own country.

    3. 03

      Cross-border corridors

      The same trade record adds export steps for trade between markets: contract, documents, finance, shipment, inspection and settlement.

    Our markets

    Saudi ArabiaT57's regional headquarters and largest demand market, and a growing food exporter.
    United Arab EmiratesA leading food trade and re-export hub for the Gulf, Africa and beyond.
    IndiaOne of the world's largest food producers, with millions of small farms and growing exports.
    MalaysiaA global halal hub and T57's gateway to ASEAN.
    TürkiyeA major producer of fruit, nuts, vegetables and processed food, bridging Europe, Central Asia and the Middle East.

    See each market's pages for local features, rules and how to get started.

    Trade both ways, between every market

    Every founding market is both a buyer and a seller on T57. A member in any one of them can buy from, or sell to, verified members in all the others, on the same trade record. For example:

    Saudi Arabia ↔ IndiaRice, spices, fresh produce and meat to the Kingdom; Saudi dates and processed food to India.
    Saudi Arabia ↔ MalaysiaHalal processed food and palm products to the Kingdom; Saudi dates to Malaysia and ASEAN.
    Saudi Arabia ↔ TürkiyeFruit, nuts, vegetables and pasta to the Kingdom; Saudi dates and dairy to Türkiye.
    UAE ↔ all marketsImports from India, Malaysia and Türkiye for the UAE and for re-export, and UAE re-exports onward.
    India ↔ Malaysia ↔ TürkiyeSpices, rice, palm products, pulses, nuts and processed food moving between producing markets.

    Regional programs

    OIC and IOFST57's founding team worked with the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS), the OIC's food security institution, and T57 has a 10-year MoU with IOFS. IOFS links T57 to OIC member states across Asia, the Middle East and Africa.ASEANFrom Malaysia, T57 opens halal food and palm corridors between Southeast Asia, the Gulf and India.
    AfricaAfrica spent more than $83 billion importing food in 2023 (UN Economic Commission for Africa). Through IOFS, African importers can source from verified suppliers in T57's markets, and African producers can reach buyers in the Gulf and Asia. T57 is in discussions with the African Development Bank on a pilot in Africa.

    More markets will join the network as T57 grows.

    Why T57

    We believe that a food trade network must be global in reach and local in practice.

    Local teams in every founding marketSales, onboarding, verification and support staff work in each country.
    Institutional reachT57 works with institutions across the OIC, ASEAN and Africa, including a 10-year MoU with the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS), and has more than 150 MoUs and letters of intent from 67 countries.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Which countries does T57 operate in?

    Saudi Arabia, the UAE, India, Malaysia and Türkiye. More markets will follow.

    Can I trade with a country that is not a T57 market?

    Members in founding markets can buy from or sell to verified members in other founding markets.

    Does T57 support domestic trade, or only exports?

    Both. Domestic wholesale and cross-border trade run on the same platform.

    Markets · OIC & HALAL

    Halal trade across the OIC, verified end to end.

    Connect halal food producers and buyers across the OIC on one trusted network.

    Join the halal trade networkSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. Halal proofWithout T57: Certificates hard to checkWith T57: Recorded, with issuer and expiry
    2. PartnersWithout T57: Distant intermediariesWith T57: Direct, verified suppliers
    3. FinanceWithout T57: Out of reachWith T57: Through licensed partners

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 exists to make halal food trade across OIC member countries faster, safer and easier to verify, from certified producer to final buyer.

    The challenge

    The challenge

    Muslim consumers spent an estimated $1.5 trillion on food in 2024, and that figure is projected to reach $2.1 trillion by 2029 (DinarStandard, State of the Global Islamic Economy 2025/26). Yet trade between OIC countries still struggles with fragmented halal certification, limited trust between new partners, and producers who cannot reach buyers or finance in other member states. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Halal assurance

    Buyers need proof that certificates are genuine, current and recognized in their market.

    Limited intra-OIC links

    Producers and buyers in member countries often trade through distant intermediaries.

    Access to finance

    Small producers and traders lack finance, including Shariah-compliant options.

    How T57 works for OIC trade

    1. 01

      Join and verify

      Producers, traders and buyers are verified, with halal certificates recorded on their Passport.

    2. 02

      Find partners

      Buyers find verified halal suppliers across member countries by product, certification and role.

    3. 03

      Trade on one record

      Contracts, halal and health certificates, inspection and shipping documents sit on one record.

    4. 04

      Finance and settle

      Licensed partners provide escrow, letters of credit and finance, including Shariah-compliant options where available.

    Features active in OIC markets

    Halal certificate recordsCertificates recorded on the Passport with issuer and expiry. For buyers, this means verified halal supply.
    Certificate expiry alertsReminders before certificates lapse. For producers, this keeps exports moving.
    Destination requirementsThe documents each OIC destination requires, by product. For exporters, this means fewer rejections.
    Verified supplier searchFilter by product, country, role and certification. For importers, this means direct access to the source.
    Trade finance through partnersEscrow, letters of credit and finance from licensed partners, including Islamic finance.
    Arabic and local languagesThe platform and AI assistants work in Arabic and other local languages.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Malaysian halal food maker reaches buyers in Saudi Arabia

    A Selangor maker of halal frozen foods wants to enter the Saudi market. On T57, its JAKIM halal certificate is recorded on its Passport, and the platform shows the documents Saudi Arabia requires. A verified Riyadh distributor finds it, agrees terms on T57 and pays through a letter of credit from a partner bank.

    Why T57

    We believe that trade between OIC nations should be as easy as trade within them.

    Born from OIC food security workT57's founding team saw the gaps in access to markets, technology and finance through its work with the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS), with which T57 has a 10-year MoU.
    Reaching AfricaMany IOFS member states are in Africa, which spent more than $83 billion importing food in 2023 (UN Economic Commission for Africa). Through IOFS, African importers can buy from verified halal suppliers in T57's markets, and African producers can sell to buyers in the Gulf and Asia. T57 is in discussions with the African Development Bank on a pilot in Africa.
    Trust layer for halal tradeVerified members, recorded certificates and one trade record give buyers confidence in what they buy.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Does T57 issue halal certificates?

    No. Halal certificates are issued by accredited halal bodies. T57 records them, tracks expiry and shows them to buyers.

    Which OIC countries can use T57?

    T57's founding markets include Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Malaysia and Türkiye, all OIC members, and India, a major supplier to OIC markets. More OIC countries will follow.

    Is Islamic trade finance available?

    T57 connects members with licensed partners, including those offering Shariah-compliant finance where available.

    Markets · ASEAN

    Southeast Asian food, to the Gulf and India.

    Link Southeast Asian food producers to buyers across Asia and the Gulf.

    Join T57 in ASEANSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. BuyersWithout T57: Far away, through agentsWith T57: Matched by corridor
    2. DocumentsWithout T57: Courier and emailWith T57: Digital, on one record
    3. FinanceWithout T57: Gaps while goods travelWith T57: Through licensed partners

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 connects ASEAN food producers and traders, starting from Malaysia, to verified buyers in the Gulf, India and Türkiye, on a trade record built for digital trade rules.

    The challenge

    The challenge

    Southeast Asia is a major supplier of rice, palm oil, seafood, fruit and halal processed food. ASEAN is also moving toward common digital trade rules: negotiations on the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) concluded in May 2026, with signing targeted for November 2026. Yet many ASEAN producers still rely on intermediaries to reach distant buyers, and cross-border paperwork remains slow. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Distance from buyers

    Producers rarely deal directly with buyers in the Gulf or South Asia.

    Paper-based trade

    Documents still move by courier and email.

    Finance gaps

    Small exporters struggle to fund orders while they wait for payment.

    How T57 works in ASEAN

    1. 01

      Join through Malaysia

      Members onboard with T57's Malaysia team, T57's hub for ASEAN.

    2. 02

      Verify and list

      Producers are verified, with halal and food-safety certificates recorded.

    3. 03

      Trade on corridors

      Halal food, palm products and other goods flow to the Gulf and India, and Gulf products such as dates flow back.

    4. 04

      Finance and settle

      Licensed partners provide escrow, letters of credit and trade finance.

    Features active in ASEAN

    Halal and food-safety certificatesRecorded on the Passport. For buyers, this proves compliance.
    Corridor matchingBuyers in the Gulf, India and Türkiye matched with ASEAN suppliers. For exporters, this opens new markets.
    Digital trade documentsDocuments generated and shared on one record. For traders, this means faster clearance.
    Trade finance through partnersFor exporters, this means funding while goods are in transit.
    Supply intelligenceSupply status by origin (surplus, stable, at risk, shortage). For buyers, this means earlier warnings.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Saudi date exporter finds buyers in Malaysia

    A date producer in Al-Qassim wants to sell more in Southeast Asia ahead of Ramadan. On T57, it is matched with verified Malaysian importers and wholesalers, agrees terms and ships with documents on one record. Payment is held in escrow by a licensed partner and released on delivery.

    Why T57

    Local in practice, global in reach

    A partner in ASEANT57 has a strategic partnership in ASEAN, aligned with the region's digital economy agenda.
    Built for digital tradeT57's trade record, electronic documents and consent-based data sharing match the direction of ASEAN's digital trade rules.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Which ASEAN countries can use T57?

    Malaysia is a founding market. Other ASEAN countries will follow.

    Can ASEAN producers sell within ASEAN?

    Yes. Domestic wholesale is available in Malaysia, and cross-border trade grows as more ASEAN markets join.

    How does T57 relate to DEFA?

    T57 is an independent platform. Its digital records and consent-based data sharing are designed to fit regional digital trade rules such as DEFA, once in force.

    Trade food in Saudi Arabia, at home and abroad.

    Trade food in Saudi Arabia with verified partners, at home and abroad.

    Get started in Saudi ArabiaSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. PartnersWithout T57: Unverified, through agentsWith T57: Verified, at home and abroad
    2. PaperworkWithout T57: Separate for every borderWith T57: One record, export steps added
    3. FinanceWithout T57: Hard to getWith T57: Licensed local partners

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 gives Saudi producers, manufacturers, traders and buyers one verified network for domestic wholesale and cross-border food trade.

    The challenge

    Saudi Arabia is T57's regional headquarters and its largest demand market.

    It imports much of its food, and it is also a growing exporter: Saudi date exports reached SAR 1.938 billion in 2025, up 14.3% on the year before, to more than 125 countries (Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture). Yet many small producers and cooperatives still sell through intermediaries and struggle to reach business buyers, export markets and working capital. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Reaching business buyers

    Small producers find it hard to sell directly to supermarkets, hotels and institutions.

    Secure imports

    Importers need verified suppliers and alternative origins when supply is disrupted.

    Working capital

    Small businesses struggle to finance trade.

    How T57 works in Saudi Arabia

    1. 01

      Join

      Apply online or with T57's Riyadh team.

    2. 02

      Verify

      KYC, KYB and, for producers, a site visit by the local team.

    3. 03

      Trade

      Sell to domestic business buyers or trade across borders on one record.

    4. 04

      Grow

      Use finance, logistics and insurance from licensed local partners.

    Features active in Saudi Arabia

    All T57 capabilities are available, with local partners. See Features available in Saudi Arabia.

    Trade both ways with Saudi Arabia

    Saudi members can buy from and sell to verified members in every founding market:

    IndiaBuy rice, spices, fresh produce and meat; sell dates and processed food.
    MalaysiaBuy halal processed food and palm products; sell dates into Malaysia and ASEAN.
    TürkiyeBuy fruit, nuts, vegetables and pasta; sell dates and dairy.
    UAETrade with the Gulf's main re-export hub, in both directions.
    Africa, through IOFSReach African importers and producers in OIC member states.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Madinah date cooperative sells direct to hotel groups

    A date cooperative near Madinah joins T57 with its member growers. Verified as an owner-producer, it sells directly to hotel groups and caterers in Riyadh and Jeddah on wholesale terms, and ships its first export order to a verified importer in Malaysia.

    Why T57 in Saudi Arabia

    Local in practice, global in reach

    Regional headquartersT57's regional headquarters is in Riyadh, with a local team for sales, onboarding, verification and support.
    Trust layerVerified members, one trade record and licensed local partners for regulated services.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Who can join T57 in Saudi Arabia?

    Registered food and agriculture businesses, from producers and cooperatives to traders, wholesalers, retailers, hotels, restaurants and institutions.

    Do I need to export to use T57?

    No. Many members use T57 for domestic wholesale only.

    Is T57 available in Arabic?

    Yes.

    Markets · Saudi Arabia · Regulatory guide

    Know the rules before you ship.

    Know the rules for food trade in Saudi Arabia before you ship.

    Check requirements for your productSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. RequirementsWithout T57: Found out at the borderWith T57: A checklist on every trade
    2. MistakesWithout T57: Delays and rejectionsWith T57: Flagged before you ship
    3. CertificatesWithout T57: Lapse unnoticedWith T57: Tracked with expiry alerts

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's regulatory guide summarizes the main bodies, documents and rules for food trade in Saudi Arabia, and shows on each trade what is required.

    The challenge

    The challenge

    Food shipments are held at borders every day because of a missing certificate, a wrong label or an unregistered product. Rules differ by country and by product, and they change. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Complex requirements

    Different documents for each product and destination.

    Changing rules

    Requirements are updated often.

    Costly mistakes

    Errors mean delays, rejections and spoiled goods.

    Key bodies and rules in Saudi Arabia

    Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA)Regulates food safety, product registration and import requirements.
    Halal certificationHalal certificates are required for products such as meat and poultry, from bodies recognized by the SFDA.
    Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA)Customs clearance and duties, and electronic invoicing (FATOORA) for VAT-registered businesses.
    FASAHThe national single window for import and export procedures.
    Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL)Governs how personal data is handled.

    How T57 helps you comply

    1. 01

      Requirement checklists

      On each trade, T57 lists the documents needed for the product and destination.

    2. 02

      Document checks

      AI flags missing or mismatched documents for a person to review.

    3. 03

      Certificate tracking

      Licences, halal and health certificates are tracked with expiry alerts.

    4. 04

      Partner support

      Customs brokers and inspectors connected to the trade record.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Is this guide legal advice?

    No. It is a summary to help you prepare. Always confirm requirements with the relevant authority or your customs broker.

    How often is the guide updated?

    T57 reviews it regularly.

    Can T57 handle customs clearance for me?

    T57 connects you with licensed customs brokers, who handle clearance on the shared trade record.

    Markets · UAE

    Trade through the UAE hub, with verified partners.

    Trade food through the UAE with verified partners across the region.

    Get started in the UAESee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. PartnersWithout T57: Unverified, through agentsWith T57: Verified, at home and abroad
    2. PaperworkWithout T57: Separate for every borderWith T57: One record, export steps added
    3. FinanceWithout T57: Hard to getWith T57: Licensed local partners

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 gives UAE importers, re-exporters, distributors, retailers and food service businesses one verified network for domestic wholesale and cross-border food trade.

    The challenge

    The challenge

    The UAE is one of the world's great trading hubs: its non-oil foreign trade reached about AED 3.8 trillion ($1.03 trillion) in 2025, up about 27% on the year before (WAM). It imports most of its food, and its traders supply markets across the Gulf, Africa and Asia. Speed and trust matter, because food is perishable and margins are thin. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Supplier risk

    Importers need verified suppliers and alternative origins at short notice.

    Working capital

    Traders tie up cash in goods in transit.

    Document load

    Re-exports multiply the documents and checks each shipment needs.

    How T57 works in the UAE

    1. 01

      Join

      Apply online or with T57's UAE team.

    2. 02

      Verify

      KYC, KYB and site checks by the local team.

    3. 03

      Trade

      Buy, sell and re-export on one record, with domestic wholesale for hotels, restaurants, caterers and retailers.

    4. 04

      Grow

      Use finance, escrow, insurance and logistics from licensed UAE partners.

    Trade both ways with the UAE

    IndiaBuy rice, spices, fresh produce and meat; re-export onward, or sell UAE-processed food back.
    Saudi ArabiaTwo-way trade across the Gulf, from dates and dairy to imported goods.
    MalaysiaBuy halal processed food and palm products for the UAE and for re-export.
    TürkiyeBuy fruit, nuts, vegetables and processed food; sell re-exported goods.
    Africa, through IOFSSupply African importers from the UAE hub, and source African produce for the Gulf.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Dubai hotel group buys direct from local and Indian growers

    A Dubai hotel group buys hydroponic leafy greens from a verified UAE farm on weekly wholesale terms, and imports mangoes for the summer season from a verified farmer producer organization in India. Both trades run on one T57 account, with one set of records for its procurement and finance teams.

    Why T57 in the UAE

    Local in practice, global in reach

    Built for a trading hubOne record for import, domestic sale and re-export, with licensed partners for finance and payments.
    Trust layerVerified members, recorded certificates and an audit trail on every trade.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Can free zone companies join?

    Yes. Mainland and free zone companies can apply, subject to verification.

    Do I need to export to use T57?

    No. Many members use T57 for domestic wholesale only.

    Is T57 available in Arabic?

    Yes, in Arabic and English.

    Markets · India

    India's farms and food makers, to buyers at home and abroad.

    Connect India's farmers and food makers to verified buyers at home and abroad.

    Get started in IndiaSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. PartnersWithout T57: Unverified, through agentsWith T57: Verified, at home and abroad
    2. PaperworkWithout T57: Separate for every borderWith T57: One record, export steps added
    3. FinanceWithout T57: Hard to getWith T57: Licensed local partners

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 gives Indian farmer producer organizations, cooperatives, processors and exporters one verified network to sell to domestic business buyers and to importers in the Gulf, Southeast Asia and beyond.

    The challenge

    The challenge

    India is one of the world's largest food producers, and its agricultural exports reached $52.55 billion in FY2025–26 (Ministry of Commerce and Industry). Yet most of its farms are small, and many producers still sell through layers of intermediaries, with little view of the final price, limited access to export buyers and little working capital. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Distance from buyers

    Farmers and FPOs rarely deal directly with business buyers or importers.

    Proof of quality and origin

    Overseas buyers need verified suppliers and documents they can trust.

    Working capital

    Small exporters wait months to be paid.

    How T57 works in India

    1. 01

      Join

      Apply online, through your FPO or cooperative, or with T57's India team.

    2. 02

      Verify

      KYC, KYB and a site visit for producers.

    3. 03

      Trade

      Sell to supermarkets, hotels, processors and institutions in India, or export on one record.

    4. 04

      Grow

      Use finance, insurance, inspection and logistics from licensed Indian partners.

    Trade both ways with India

    Saudi Arabia and the UAESell rice, spices, fresh produce, meat and processed food; buy dates and Gulf processed food.
    Malaysia and ASEANSell rice, spices and vegetables; buy palm products and halal processed food.
    TürkiyeSell spices, rice and tea; buy nuts, dried fruit and pulses.
    Africa, through IOFSSell rice, pulses, spices and processed food to African importers, and buy African produce such as cashews and pulses. T57 is in discussions with the African Development Bank on a pilot in Africa.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Nashik farmer producer organization exports grapes to the Gulf

    An FPO of grape growers in Nashik, Maharashtra, joins T57 and is verified as an owner-producer. It sells part of its harvest to a supermarket chain in Mumbai on wholesale terms, and exports the rest to a verified importer in Riyadh, with an inspection partner's report and the phytosanitary certificate on the trade record. A partner bank finances the export invoice, and payment is released from escrow on delivery.

    Why T57 in India

    Local in practice, global in reach

    Built with IndiaT57's technology team works in India, and the platform supports onboarding through FPOs and cooperatives.
    Trust layerVerified members, recorded certificates and one trade record that buyers and banks can rely on.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Can a farmer producer organization join?

    Yes. FPOs and cooperatives can join as members and onboard their member farmers.

    Is T57 only for exporters?

    No. Many members use T57 to sell to domestic business buyers.

    Which languages are supported?

    English and Hindi, with more Indian languages planned.

    Markets · India · Regulatory guide

    Know the rules before you ship.

    Know the rules for food trade in India before you ship.

    Check requirements for your productSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. RequirementsWithout T57: Found out at the borderWith T57: A checklist on every trade
    2. MistakesWithout T57: Delays and rejectionsWith T57: Flagged before you ship
    3. CertificatesWithout T57: Lapse unnoticedWith T57: Tracked with expiry alerts

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's regulatory guide summarizes the main bodies, documents and rules for food trade in India, and shows on each trade what is required.

    The challenge

    The challenge

    Food shipments are held at borders every day because of a missing certificate, a wrong label or an unregistered product. Rules differ by country and by product, and they change. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Complex requirements

    Different documents for each product and destination.

    Changing rules

    Requirements are updated often.

    Costly mistakes

    Errors mean delays, rejections and spoiled goods.

    Key bodies and rules in India

    Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT)Importer Exporter Code (IEC) for anyone who imports or exports.
    APEDA and other export promotion councilsRegistration for exporters of scheduled agricultural and processed food products.
    Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)Food business licensing and clearance of food imports.
    Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage (PPQS)Phytosanitary certificates for plant products.
    Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)Customs clearance through ICEGATE, and GST, including e-invoicing for eligible businesses.
    Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023Governs personal data.

    How T57 helps you comply

    1. 01

      Requirement checklists

      On each trade, T57 lists the documents needed for the product and destination.

    2. 02

      Document checks

      AI flags missing or mismatched documents for a person to review.

    3. 03

      Certificate tracking

      Licences, halal and health certificates are tracked with expiry alerts.

    4. 04

      Partner support

      Customs brokers and inspectors connected to the trade record.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Is this guide legal advice?

    No. It is a summary to help you prepare. Always confirm requirements with the relevant authority or your customs broker.

    How often is the guide updated?

    T57 reviews it regularly.

    Can T57 handle customs clearance for me?

    T57 connects you with licensed customs brokers, who handle clearance on the shared trade record.

    Markets · Malaysia

    Malaysian halal food, to buyers across three regions.

    Take Malaysian halal food to verified buyers across the Gulf, India and ASEAN.

    Get started in MalaysiaSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. PartnersWithout T57: Unverified, through agentsWith T57: Verified, at home and abroad
    2. PaperworkWithout T57: Separate for every borderWith T57: One record, export steps added
    3. FinanceWithout T57: Hard to getWith T57: Licensed local partners

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 gives Malaysian producers, halal food manufacturers, traders and buyers one verified network for domestic wholesale and cross-border trade, and is T57's gateway to ASEAN.

    The challenge

    Malaysia is a global halal hub.

    Its halal exports reached RM68.52 billion in 2025, up 10.9%, and food and beverages made up RM36.86 billion of that (Halal Development Corporation). Yet many small and mid-sized makers still find it hard to reach buyers in the Gulf and South Asia directly, or to finance large orders. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Reaching distant buyers

    SMEs rely on agents and trade shows to find importers.

    Proving halal and quality

    Buyers want certificates they can verify.

    Financing growth

    Larger export orders need working capital.

    How T57 works in Malaysia

    1. 01

      Join

      Apply online or with T57's Malaysia team.

    2. 02

      Verify

      KYC, KYB and a site visit, with halal certificates recorded on the Passport.

    3. 03

      Trade

      Sell to retailers, hotels and food service in Malaysia, or export to the Gulf, India and ASEAN on one record.

    4. 04

      Grow

      Use finance, including Islamic finance, plus insurance and logistics from licensed Malaysian partners.

    Trade both ways with Malaysia

    Saudi Arabia and the UAESell halal processed food, seafood and palm products; buy dates and Gulf processed food.
    IndiaSell palm products and processed food; buy rice, spices and vegetables.
    TürkiyeSell palm products and halal food; buy nuts, dried fruit and confectionery.
    ASEANMalaysia is T57's gateway for Southeast Asian supply and demand.
    Africa, through IOFSSell halal food and palm products to African importers in OIC member states.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Sabah seafood processor ships to Dubai

    A frozen seafood processor in Sabah, with a JAKIM halal certificate and an HACCP certificate recorded on its T57 Passport, is matched with a verified Dubai importer. The importer pays through a letter of credit from a partner bank, and the processor tracks the cold-chain shipment and documents on one record.

    Why T57 in Malaysia

    Local in practice, global in reach

    Gateway to ASEANMalaysia is T57's hub for Southeast Asia, aligned with ASEAN's digital trade agenda.
    Built for halal tradeHalal certificates are recorded, tracked and shown to buyers on every trade.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Does T57 recognize JAKIM certification?

    T57 records halal certificates from JAKIM and other bodies, and shows buyers whether a certificate is recognized in their market.

    Is Islamic trade finance available?

    Through licensed partners, where available.

    Is T57 available in Malay?

    English and Malay.

    Markets · Türkiye

    Türkiye's fruit, nuts and food, to the Gulf and Asia.

    Sell Türkiye's fruit, nuts and food products to verified buyers across the Gulf and Asia.

    Get started in TürkiyeSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. PartnersWithout T57: Unverified, through agentsWith T57: Verified, at home and abroad
    2. PaperworkWithout T57: Separate for every borderWith T57: One record, export steps added
    3. FinanceWithout T57: Hard to getWith T57: Licensed local partners

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 gives Turkish producers, processors, exporters and buyers one verified network for domestic wholesale and cross-border food trade.

    The challenge

    Türkiye is a major producer of fruit, nuts, vegetables, pulses and processed food.

    Its agricultural exports exceeded a record $36.4 billion in 2025 (Turkish Exporters Assembly). It sits between Europe, Central Asia and the Middle East, yet many smaller exporters still depend on agents and fragmented paperwork to reach Gulf and Asian buyers. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Reaching new markets

    Exporters want direct access to buyers beyond their traditional markets.

    Perishable timing

    Fresh produce needs fast, accurate documents to clear borders.

    Payment risk

    New buyers in distant markets bring payment risk.

    How T57 works in Türkiye

    1. 01

      Join

      Apply online or with T57's Türkiye team.

    2. 02

      Verify

      KYC, KYB and a site visit for producers.

    3. 03

      Trade

      Sell to retailers, hotels and processors in Türkiye, or export on one record.

    4. 04

      Grow

      Use finance, escrow, insurance and logistics from licensed Turkish partners.

    Trade both ways with Türkiye

    Saudi Arabia and the UAESell fruit, nuts, vegetables, pasta and poultry; buy dates and Gulf processed food.
    IndiaSell nuts, dried fruit and pulses; buy spices, rice and tea.
    Malaysia and ASEANSell nuts, dried fruit and confectionery; buy palm products and halal processed food.
    Africa, through IOFSSell flour, pasta and processed food to African importers, and buy African produce.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A Mersin citrus exporter enters the Saudi market

    A lemon and mandarin exporter in Mersin is matched with a verified supermarket buyer in Jeddah. T57 lists the documents Saudi Arabia requires for fresh citrus, flags a mismatch between the packing list and the phytosanitary certificate before loading, and the buyer pays into escrow through a licensed partner. The exporter ships weekly through the season.

    Why T57 in Türkiye

    Local in practice, global in reach

    A bridge between regionsTürkiye links T57's network to Europe, Central Asia and the Middle East.
    Trust layerVerified members, one trade record and licensed partners for payments.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Can Turkish companies trade in USD or EUR?

    Yes, through licensed payment and escrow partners, in any currency they support.

    Is halal certification needed for Gulf exports?

    For some products, yes. T57 shows the requirements for each product and destination.

    Is T57 available in Turkish?

    English and Turkish.

    Escrow and paymentsThrough licensed partners, in TRY and any currency the partner supports.
    InsuranceCargo and trade credit cover from licensed insurers.
    Logistics and inspectionFreight, forwarding and inspection partners, booked from the trade record.

    LanguageEnglish and Turkish.

    Yes. The partners that deliver regulated services differ by country.

    Can I pay in TRY?

    Yes, through licensed payment and escrow partners.

    Who provides finance in Türkiye?

    Licensed Turkish banks, including participation banks. T57 does not lend.

    Markets · Türkiye · Regulatory guide

    Know the rules before you ship.

    Know the rules for food trade in Türkiye before you ship.

    Check requirements for your productSee how it works

    What you get with T57

    1. RequirementsWithout T57: Found out at the borderWith T57: A checklist on every trade
    2. MistakesWithout T57: Delays and rejectionsWith T57: Flagged before you ship
    3. CertificatesWithout T57: Lapse unnoticedWith T57: Tracked with expiry alerts

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's regulatory guide summarizes the main bodies, documents and rules for food trade in Türkiye, and shows on each trade what is required.

    The challenge

    The challenge

    Food shipments are held at borders every day because of a missing certificate, a wrong label or an unregistered product. Rules differ by country and by product, and they change. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Complex requirements

    Different documents for each product and destination.

    Changing rules

    Requirements are updated often.

    Costly mistakes

    Errors mean delays, rejections and spoiled goods.

    Key bodies and rules in Türkiye

    Ministry of Agriculture and ForestryFood safety, import controls and export health and phytosanitary certificates.
    Ministry of TradeCustoms procedures, through the BILGE customs system, and export rules.
    Halal Accreditation Agency (HAK)Accreditation of halal certification bodies.
    Revenue Administration (GİB)Electronic invoicing (e-Fatura and e-Arşiv) for eligible businesses.
    Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)Governs personal data.

    How T57 helps you comply

    1. 01

      Requirement checklists

      On each trade, T57 lists the documents needed for the product and destination.

    2. 02

      Document checks

      AI flags missing or mismatched documents for a person to review.

    3. 03

      Certificate tracking

      Licences, halal and health certificates are tracked with expiry alerts.

    4. 04

      Partner support

      Customs brokers and inspectors connected to the trade record.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Is this guide legal advice?

    No. It is a summary to help you prepare. Always confirm requirements with the relevant authority or your customs broker.

    How often is the guide updated?

    T57 reviews it regularly.

    Can T57 handle customs clearance for me?

    T57 connects you with licensed customs brokers, who handle clearance on the shared trade record.

    What you get with T57

    1. MembershipWithout T57: Hidden costs and lead feesWith T57: From $199 a month, published

    3. Try firstWithout T57: Pay before you see itWith T57: 90 days free at launch

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57's pricing is simple and public: a monthly membership that gives you verified access to the network, and a small fee per side only when a trade is completed.

    The problem

    Why pricing matters

    Food businesses already pay for trade in many hidden ways: agents' margins, repeated document checks, bank charges, failed shipments and time spent chasing partners. Many platforms add listing fees or charge for leads that never become trades. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Hidden costs

    Middlemen's margins and repeated paperwork that never appear on an invoice.

    Paying for nothing

    Fees for listings and leads that do not lead to trade.

    One size for all

    Pricing that ignores the size of the business and the market it works in.

    How T57 pricing works

    Membership, verification, then a small fee only when you trade

    1. 01

      Choose a membership

      Explore from $199 a month, Core $499, Growth $749, or Enterprise from $1,499. Pay annually and get two months free.

    2. 02

      Get verified

      Your membership includes KYC and KYB verification and your reusable T57 Passport.

    3. 03

      Trade

      A small fee per side applies only when a trade is completed, from 0.75% on Explore down to 0.20% on Enterprise. Listing, quoting and negotiating are free.

    4. 04

      Add services as you need them

      Finance, insurance, logistics and inspection partners quote for their own services.

    A $20,000 trade on Core× 0.60% per side= $120 for each side
