    Why T57

    We believe that you should pay for trade that happens, not for the promise of it.

    Prices in the openMembership prices and trade fees are published, and partner charges are shown before you accept them.
    Fair across marketsLocal prices reflect each country's purchasing power, so smaller businesses in every market can afford to join.
    Trusted by institutionsT57 works with the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS) and institutions across the OIC and ASEAN.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    Do I pay to list products or send quotes?

    No. Listing, quoting and negotiating are included in your membership. The trade fee applies only when a trade is completed.

    Does T57 earn anything from finance or insurance?

    Yes. T57 earns a small commission from some finance and insurance partners. It is disclosed before you accept a partner's offer.

    Are prices the same in every country?

    The prices shown are standard list prices in US dollars. Local prices may be lower in markets with lower purchasing power. Contact us for pricing in your country.

    Is there a free trial?

    Yes. Founding members get 90 days free at launch. The trial lets you explore the network and tools. Trading starts once you subscribe and are verified.

    Pricing · Governments & Institutions

    Food-security programs, designed with you.

    Programs that strengthen your country's food security, designed with you.

    Talk to our government teamSee the government module

    What you get with T57

    1. ProducersWithout T57: Outside formal tradeWith T57: Subsidized, verified members
    2. TendersWithout T57: Exposed to leakageWith T57: One traceable record
    3. IntelligenceWithout T57: Months-old dataWith T57: AI early warning in days

    TodayWith T57

    Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

    T57 works with ministries, food-security agencies and development partners on programs that bring producers into verified trade, run public tenders on secure rails, and give governments AI-driven food-security intelligence.

    The problem

    Every country's priorities are different.

    One ministry of agriculture wants its farmers and cooperatives to reach new buyers. Another ministry wants to grow food manufacturing, or develop small businesses. A food-security agency needs early warning of supply shocks. Public procurement needs clean, traceable tenders. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

    Late information

    Food-security decisions made on old, aggregate data.

    Excluded producers

    Smallholders, cooperatives and small businesses left outside formal trade and finance.

    Opaque procurement

    Large food tenders exposed to leakage, fraud, delays and quality failures.

    How government programs work

    Define the goal with the right ministry → Design the program → Deliver → Measure

    1. 01

      Define the goal with the right ministry

      Agriculture, industry, trade, SME development or food security, depending on the country.

    2. 02

      Design the program

      Scope, markets, data permissions and funding, including memberships the government pays for on behalf of its producers and businesses.

    3. 03

      Deliver

      T57's country team onboards and verifies members, and tenders and trade run on the platform.

    4. 04

      Measure

      The government module reports agreed, aggregated results on producers reached, trade completed, prices and supply.

    What governments can do on T57

    Programs that fit national plans

    Subsidized membershipsA ministry subscribes on behalf of farmers, cooperatives or SMEs, as a direct form of support.For governments, this means measurable reach.
    Programs by priorityProducer inclusion, investment in food manufacturing, SME development and export growth.For ministries, this means programs that fit national plans.
    Public tenders, local and globalPublish food tenders on T57, invite verified suppliers from home or abroad, and evaluate, award and pay on one traceable record, with escrow through licensed partners.For procurement teams, this means clean, auditable buying.
    Government moduleFood-security dashboards and index, supply status and surplus or deficit by origin, AI early warning, and scenario modeling for tariffs, quotas, subsidies and stocks.For agencies, this means seeing shocks in days, not months.
    Government-to-government tradeSupply arrangements and emergency corridors between states, on the same verified record.For ministries, this means faster agreements.
    Co-funded programs with development partnersPrograms can be designed with multilateral development banks, UN agencies and agricultural development funds. T57 is in discussions with the World Bank and the African Development Bank.For partners, this means verified, measurable impact.
    Permissioned data onlyNo individual member data is shared without consent.

    Use case · Illustrative example

    A ministry of agriculture subsidizes cooperatives into export trade

    A ministry of agriculture pays for T57 memberships for 200 date and vegetable cooperatives for their first two years. T57's country team verifies them and trains their staff, and the cooperatives start selling to domestic hotel groups and to importers in other founding markets. The ministry's dashboard shows the number of cooperatives trading, the volume and value of their sales, and the prices they receive.

    Why T57

    Why members choose T57

    Rooted in food securityT57's founding team worked with the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS), with which T57 has a 10-year MoU.
    Built for public trustVerified suppliers, an audit trail, tamper-evident records and permissioned data.
    AI advises, people decideThe government module informs policy, and officials make the decisions.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    How is government pricing set?

    By program, based on scope, number of members, markets and modules. Contact our institutional team for a proposal.

    Can a ministry pay for its farmers' memberships?

    Yes. Governments and development partners can fund memberships and onboarding for farmers, cooperatives and SMEs.

    Can foreign suppliers respond to our tenders?

    Yes, if you open a tender to them. Every supplier is verified before it can bid.

    Glossary

    26 terms, in plain language

    ABCEHIKLOPST
    AI advises, people decide
    T57's principle for AI. AI makes recommendations, and a person reviews every adverse decision, with a stated reason and a route to contest it. On T57 →
    Beneficial owner
    The person who ultimately owns or controls a company, even if the shares are held through other companies.
    Bill of lading (B/L)
    A document issued by a carrier that receipts the goods, sets out the terms of carriage and, in most forms, gives title to the goods.
    Certificate of origin
    A document that states the country where goods were produced, used to apply duties and trade agreements.
    Cold chain
    Temperature-controlled storage and transport that keeps perishable food safe from producer to buyer.
    Cooperative / FPO
    A group of producers that sells, buys or works together. In India, a farmer producer organization (FPO) is a registered group of farmers.
    Corridor
    A regular trade route between a supplying market and a buying market, such as India to Saudi Arabia. On T57 →
    Escrow
    An arrangement where a licensed third party holds the buyer's payment and releases it to the seller when agreed conditions are met. On T57 →
    Halal certificate
    A certificate from an accredited halal body confirming that a product meets Islamic dietary requirements. On T57 →
    HoReCa
    Hotels, restaurants and caterers, the food service sector.
    HS code
    The Harmonized System code that classifies traded goods for customs and duties.
    Incoterms
    Standard trade terms from the International Chamber of Commerce, such as FOB or CIF, that set who pays for and bears the risk of each stage of delivery.
    Intermediary
    A business that connects buyers and sellers without producing, processing or holding the goods. T57 labels intermediaries so buyers know who they deal with.
    Invoice financing
    Finance a lender provides against an unpaid invoice, so the seller is paid before the buyer's payment is due.
    KYB (Know Your Business)
    Checks that confirm a company is real, properly registered and licensed, and who owns it. On T57 →
    KYC (Know Your Customer)
    Checks that confirm the identity of the people who own and act for a business. On T57 →
    Letter of credit (LC)
    A bank's promise to pay the seller when the seller presents documents that meet the LC's terms. On T57 →
    Owner-producer
    A member that grows, raises, catches or makes the goods it sells, with ownership verified by T57.
    Phytosanitary certificate
    A government certificate confirming that plants or plant products meet the importing country's plant health rules.
    Sanctions screening
    Checking people and companies against government sanctions and watchlists. On T57 →
    Smart contract
    Software that carries out agreed steps automatically, such as instructing a payment partner to release funds when a delivery is confirmed.
    Supply status by origin
    T57's view of whether supply of a product from an origin is surplus, stable, at risk or in shortage. On T57 →
    T57 Passport
    A member's reusable verified profile, showing their role, checks passed and trade history, shared with consent. On T57 →
    Tokenized trade document
    A trade document, such as an invoice or warehouse receipt, issued as a unique digital token so it cannot be duplicated or financed twice. On T57 →
    Trade finance gap
    The value of trade finance that businesses request but cannot get. The Asian Development Bank estimated it at $2.5 trillion in 2025. On T57 →
    Trade record
    The single shared record of a trade on T57, from quote to settlement, that every party sees. On T57 →

    No term matches. Try another word, or ask the Help Center.

    FAQ

    Common questions

    What is T57?

    T57 is AI-native digital trade infrastructure for the entire food ecosystem. It is a members-only trade club where verified producers, processors, traders and buyers trade on one shared record, with finance, insurance, logistics and inspection from licensed partners.

    Is T57 a marketplace?

    No. On an open marketplace, anyone can list. On T57, every member is verified before they trade, and their role is checked and shown.

    Does T57 buy or sell food?

    No. T57 does not own goods, lend money, hold client funds or provide transport. Members trade with each other, and licensed partners provide regulated services.

    Which countries does T57 operate in?

    Saudi Arabia, the UAE, India, Malaysia and Türkiye, with more markets to follow.

      FAQ

      Common questions

      How long does the free trial last?

      Founding members get 90 days free at launch. After the launch period, the trial is 14 days.

      Can I trade during the free trial?

      You can explore members, intelligence and AI tools, and send requests for quote. Contracts, escrow and finance start once you subscribe and are verified.

      How do I cancel or change my plan?

      From your account settings. Upgrades apply at once, and downgrades apply at renewal.

      Does T57 hold my money?

      No. Payments, escrow and letters of credit are handled by licensed partners.

      Can other members see my prices?

      No. Only the parties you quote can see your prices.

      Partnerships

      Serve verified food businesses, inside the trade itself.

      Partner with the network that food trade runs on.

      Become a partnerBecome a partner

      What you get with T57

      1. CustomersWithout T57: Found one by oneWith T57: Verified members, ready to buy
      2. DataWithout T57: Weak, unverifiedWith T57: The full trade record
      3. WorkflowWithout T57: Email and re-keyingWith T57: Connected by API or portal

      TodayWith T57

      Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

      T57 partners with banks, insurers, logistics and inspection providers, technology companies and institutions, so every verified trade on T57 can be financed, insured, moved and checked by trusted specialists.

      The problem

      T57 does not lend, hold client funds, own goods or provide transport.

      It connects the specialists who do. For partners, the challenge is reaching good customers in food trade at a cost that works. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

      Costly customer acquisition

      Finding and checking smaller food businesses one by one is expensive.

      Poor data

      Banks and insurers lack reliable records to price risk.

      Disconnected workflows

      Partners receive documents by email and re-key them.

      Partner types

      Four kinds of specialist, one trade record

      Financial servicesBanks, finance companies, escrow providers, insurers and takaful operators.Logistics and inspectionFreight forwarders, shipping lines, cold chain, warehouses, inspection and testing, customs brokers.TechnologyCloud, data, AI, identity and integration partners.InstitutionsGovernments, development partners and regional organizations such as the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS).

      How partnership works

      Apply → Qualify → Connect → Serve

      1. 01

        Apply

        Tell us about your services, licences and markets.

      2. 02

        Qualify

        T57 checks your licences and fit, and agrees commercial terms.

      3. 03

        Connect

        Your services are connected to the trade record, through APIs or the partner portal.

      4. 04

        Serve

        Verified members choose your offer from inside their trade.

      Why T57

      Verified customers and institutional backing

      Verified customers, ready to buyEvery member has passed KYC and KYB, and every request comes with the trade record behind it.
      Institutional backingT57 has a 10-year MoU with IOFS, an MoU with ASEAN, and more than 150 MoUs and letters of intent from companies in 67 countries. It is also in discussions with the World Bank and the African Development Bank.

      FAQ

      Common questions

      Does T57 compete with partners?

      No. T57 does not lend, insure, ship or inspect. It brings partners verified customers and better data.

      How do partners get paid?

      Members pay partners for their services directly. T57 may earn a small commission from some partners, as agreed in each partnership.

      Can partners in any country join?

      Partners licensed in T57's markets, or serving trade with them, can apply.

      About T57

      Food that exists should reach the people who need it.

      We exist so that food that exists reaches the people and markets that need it.

      Meet our teamMeet our team

      What you get with T57

      1. MarketsWithout T57: Out of reachWith T57: Verified buyers across borders
      2. TechnologyWithout T57: Paper and phone callsWith T57: One shared trade record
      3. FinanceWithout T57: Rarely reaches small firmsWith T57: Documented trades lenders can fund

      TodayWith T57

      Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

      T57 is AI-native digital trade infrastructure for the entire food ecosystem: a members-only network where verified businesses trade on one record, with finance, insurance and logistics from trusted partners.

      Our story

      One question, asked in more than 60 countries

      T57 began with one question: why does food that exists not reach the people and markets that need it? Through AlMukarramah, T57's founding team designed the strategy and ecosystem of the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS), the OIC's food security institution. Over four years, the team travelled to more than 60 countries and met ministries, buyers, sellers, processors, cooperatives and farmers. Producers, traders and governments were rarely short of food or of willing partners. They were short of three things:

      Access to markets

      Producers and small traders cannot reach or prove themselves to buyers beyond their own networks.

      Access to technology

      Trade still runs on phone calls, messages and paper, with no shared record of a deal.

      Access to finance

      Working capital rarely reaches the smaller businesses that need it most.

      How we built T57

      Studied, listened, built, launched

      60+countries visited
      150+trade and agri-food platforms studied
      350+case studies examined
      5founding markets
      1. 01

        Studied the problem

        Over three to four years, we examined more than 150 trade and agri-food platforms and more than 350 case studies worldwide. Each solved part of the problem. None connected the whole trade.

      2. 02

        Listened on the ground

        We built on what producers, traders and governments told us in more than 60 countries.

      3. 03

        Applied the latest technology

        Digital verification, connected trade records and AI, to close all three gaps together.

      4. 04

        Started where both ends are live

        We launched in five founding markets, because a corridor only works when both ends are live, and we are building for many more.

      The story behind our name

      T57 is a promise written as a name: T, the values every trade must stand on, 5 industries brought together on one record, and 7 outcomes we work to deliver for every member.

      T

      Trade, built on trust, transparency and traceability

      Trade is what we enable. Trust, transparency and traceability are how. Trust: every member is verified before they trade. Transparency: every party sees the same terms, documents and status on one record, and every AI recommendation comes with its reasons. Traceability: every trade can be followed from source to buyer, with each document and step recorded and tamper-evident.

      5

      Five industries, one trade

      A single food trade needs five industries working together. T57 connects them on one record:

      • Agriculture and food productionWhat is grown, raised, caught, processed and made.
      • TradeBuyers and sellers, at home and across borders.
      • LogisticsFreight, cold chain, warehousing, inspection and customs.
      • FinancePayments, escrow, letters of credit, trade finance and insurance.
      • TechnologyVerification, trade records, blockchain and AI.

      7

      Seven outcomes, from local trade to global food security

      1. 1Food security

        Earlier warning of shortages and more sources of supply for the communities and countries that depend on imported food.

      2. 2Less food lost

        Surplus matched to buyers before it spoils, so more of what is grown reaches people.

      3. 3Integration

        One connected food system, where producers, buyers, banks, logistics providers and governments work on the same record, and trade moves from quote to settlement in days, not weeks.

      4. 4Access to finance

        Verified, documented trades that banks can finance, helping close the trade finance gap for smaller businesses.

      5. 5Higher incomes

        Fairer prices and direct access to buyers, so more of the value of food stays with those who produce it.

      6. 6Inclusion

        Smallholders, cooperatives, women-owned businesses and SMEs brought into formal trade, finance and markets.

      7. 7Resilience

        Food systems that adapt to climate, conflict and supply shocks, with alternative origins and routes ready when they are needed.

      Trade built on trust, transparency and traceability, across five industries, delivering seven outcomes. That is T57.

      Born from food security work

      Born from food security workOur founding team designed the strategy and ecosystem of IOFS, and T57 has a 10-year MoU with IOFS.
      Shared infrastructure, not a middlemanT57 does not buy, hold or move goods, lend money or hold client funds. We connect the businesses and specialists that do.

      FAQ

      Common questions

      Where is T57 based?

      T57's operating company is in Dubai, its regional headquarters is in Riyadh, and it has teams in India and Malaysia, with country teams in all five founding markets.

      What does the name T57 mean?

      T stands for trade, built on trust, transparency and traceability. The 5 stands for the five industries T57 connects: agriculture and food production, trade, logistics, finance and technology. The 7 stands for the seven outcomes we work toward: food security, less food lost, integration, access to finance, higher incomes, inclusion and resilience.

      Who owns T57?

      T57 is founder-led.

      Founders

      Five founders

      AN
      Afzal Hussain Mohammed NakheebFounder, Chairman and Head of Strategy

      Afzal works where food security, trade and public policy meet. Over three decades he has built food, trade and enterprise systems across Saudi Arabia, the UAE and India. At T57 he leads strategy and the platform's partnerships with governments, multilateral institutions and development finance partners.

      As Founder and Chairman of Al Mukarramah, he led the team that designed the strategy and ecosystem of the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS), and in 2023 he signed a ten-year strategic implementation agreement with the organization. Since then he has signed memoranda of understanding with the Government of the Chechen Republic (2025), the Development Bank of Maldives (2026) and Kazakhstan's Food Contract Corporation (2026). He is also Chairman of AMK Holding, a Riyadh-based multi-family office that aligns patient capital with long-term economic programs.

He served as Chief Operating Officer of BMPC, the agribusiness founded by Sheikh Saleh Kamel. Earlier in his career he ran FMCG distribution for global brands in Dubai and hypermarket operations in India.

      Why it matters

      The people who feed the world are the least connected

      ⅓of the world's food comes from small farms (FAO)
      13%of food is lost between harvest and retail (FAO)
      645Mpeople faced hunger in 2025 (SOFI 2026)

      Small farms produce about a third of the world's food (FAO), yet their producers are often the least connected to buyers and finance. About 13% of food is lost between harvest and retail (FAO). And 645 million people faced hunger in 2025 (SOFI 2026).

      Our innovation principles

      Four principles

      AI advises, people decideEvery adverse decision is reviewed by a person, with a stated reason and a route to contest it.
      Small and localA family of small AI models for each region, crop and language, trained on verified trade data and farmer knowledge shared with consent.
      Trust by designVerified members, one trade record, tamper-evident anchoring and permissioned data.
      Partners, not replacementsWe connect banks, insurers, forwarders and inspectors, rather than replace them.

      The impact we work toward

      Five changes we measure ourselves against

      • Market accessSmallholders, cooperatives and SMEs reach verified buyers at home and abroad.
      • Access to financeDocumented trades that lenders can finance.
      • Less food lossSurplus signals and matching that help produce find buyers before it is lost.
      • InclusionAssisted onboarding through cooperatives, and women-owned businesses tracked and supported from onboarding.
      • Skilled jobsCountry teams and technology roles in our markets.

      Impact figures will be published as the platform reports them. None are claimed yet.

      About T57 · Food Security

      Make food security visible, verifiable and actionable.

      Make food security visible, verifiable and actionable.

      Talk to our government teamSee how it works

      What you get with T57

      1. InformationWithout T57: After prices riseWith T57: Supply status by origin
      2. SourcingWithout T57: A few originsWith T57: Verified alternatives
      3. ProducersWithout T57: ExcludedWith T57: Assisted onboarding

      TodayWith T57

      Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

      T57 strengthens food security by connecting verified producers and buyers across borders, and by turning verified trade data into early warning of where supply is at risk.

      The problem

      Import-dependent countries are exposed

      645Mpeople faced hunger in 2025 (SOFI 2026)
      136.0FAO Food Price Index, September 2026, up 5.8% on a year earlier
      20–45%of key agrifood inputs pass through the Strait of Hormuz (FAO, April 2026)

      In 2025, 645 million people faced hunger, and about 520 million are still projected to in 2030 (SOFI 2026). The FAO Food Price Index reached 136.0 in September 2026, 5.8% higher than a year earlier and the highest since November 2022. Import-dependent countries are exposed: in April 2026, FAO warned that 20 to 45% of key agrifood inputs depend on passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

      Late information

      Governments see supply problems only after prices rise.

      Narrow sourcing

      Importers depend on a few origins and intermediaries.

      Excluded producers

      Small producers cannot reach the markets that need their food.

      How T57 supports food security

      Connect, see, act, include

      1. 01

        Connect supply and demand

        Verified producers in surplus regions meet verified buyers in import-dependent markets.

      2. 02

        See supply status

        Verified trades build a live view of supply by origin: surplus, stable, at risk or shortage.

      3. 03

        Act early

        When an origin is at risk, buyers find verified alternative suppliers and routes.

      4. 04

        Include small producers

        Cooperatives and smallholders join through assisted onboarding, adding supply and earning more.

      Features

      What importers, agencies and producers get

      Supply status by originFor importers and agencies, this means earlier warning.
      Alternative supplier matchingFor importers, this means faster switching when supply is disrupted.
      Government moduleFood-security dashboards and index, surplus and deficit maps, AI early warning and scenario modeling.For ministries, this means policy based on live data.
      Public tenders and G2G tradeFor governments, this means clean, traceable buying.
      Surplus matchingFor producers, this means less food lost and better prices.
      Permissioned dataInstitutions see aggregated data only, and individual members' data stays private.

      Use case · Illustrative example

      A Gulf importer switches rice origin before shelves are affected

      A Riyadh rice importer sees on T57 that supply from its usual origin has moved to "at risk". It finds verified exporters in two other founding-market origins with surplus, compares landed costs and secures shipments before its stock runs low.

      Why T57

      Rooted in food security

      Rooted in food securityT57's founding team designed the strategy and ecosystem of the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS), and T57 has a 10-year MoU with IOFS.
      AI advises, people decideThe intelligence informs decisions. People make them.

      FAQ

      Common questions

      Is T57 a government system?

      No. T57 is an independent platform that governments and institutions can use, with permissioned data.

      What data does a government see?

      Aggregated, permissioned data on supply, prices and trade, never individual members' data without consent.

      Does T57 work only for Muslim-majority countries?

      No. T57 serves any food business or government in its markets, and works closely with IOFS and the OIC.

      About T57 · SDGs

      Verified trade, measurable progress.

      Turn verified trade into measurable progress on the Sustainable Development Goals.

      Partner with us on impact

      What you get with T57

      1. ReachWithout T57: Hard to reachWith T57: Cooperatives and SMEs onboarded
      2. ProofWithout T57: SurveysWith T57: Verified trade records
      3. SustainabilityWithout T57: Ends with fundingWith T57: Lasting market access

      TodayWith T57

      Finance, escrow and insurance come from licensed partners.

      T57 contributes to the Sustainable Development Goals by bringing small producers and businesses into verified trade and finance, and by recording that progress on a trusted record.

      The problem

      The world is off track to end hunger by 2030 (SOFI 2026).

      Development programs struggle to reach small producers at scale and to prove their impact. The key challenges T57 addresses include:

      Reach

      Programs find it hard to reach smallholders and small businesses directly.

      Proof

      Impact claims rest on surveys rather than verified records.

      Sustainability

      Support ends when funding ends, unless producers gain lasting market access.

      How T57 contributes

      Onboard → Trade → Record → Report

      1. 01

        Onboard

        Cooperatives, smallholders and SMEs join with assisted onboarding.

      2. 02

        Trade

        They sell to verified buyers and access finance through partners.

      3. 03

        Record

      Who we serve · Governments and regulators

      See your food supply. Act before shortages.

      Live trade data, food-security alerts and transparent tenders, in one view for ministries and agencies.

      Request a briefingSee how it works

      What you get with T57

      1. Food securityWithout T57: Shortages spotted too lateWith T57: Early warning of shortages
      2. Public tendersWithout T57: Paper trails, leakage riskWith T57: Transparent public tenders
      3. ProducersWithout T57: Informal and invisibleWith T57: Brought into formal trade

      TodayWith T57

      Motion graphic: food corridors light up between surplus and deficit regions

      Building real-time, governable food systems for public good

      T57 gives governments and regulators a real-time, policy-ready view of their agri and food ecosystem, linking intelligence, procurement, and capital so food security becomes a measurable, governable asset rather than a recurring crisis.

      The challenge

      Delayed data turns supply shocks into crises

      Food systems around the world are fragmented. Data is delayed, procurement is opaque, and policy often reacts to crises rather than anticipating them.

      Fragmented, slow food-security intelligence

      Ministries often rely on scattered reports, manual spreadsheets, and diplomatic emails to understand supply, demand, and risk, which makes early-warning and coordinated action difficult.

      Opaque, high-risk public procurement

      Large food tenders are vulnerable to leakage, fraud, payment delays, and quality failures, undermining public trust and budgets.

      Limited visibility to align policy, markets, and investment

      Policy decisions on trade, subsidies, storage, and investment often proceed without a clear, data-backed picture of surpluses, deficits, food waste, or SME capacity across regions and value chains.

      How T57 works for governments and regulators

      From live intelligence to clean procurement

      1. 01

        Strategic onboarding and integration

        A dashboard aligned with your food-security agenda, connected through APIs to your procurement, customs and audit systems.

      2. 02

        Live intelligence and early warning

        Live dashboards, AI early warning and "what-if" modeling of tariff, quota, subsidy and trade-route options.

      3. 03

        Clean, transparent procurement

        RFQs to vetted sellers, with smart contracts and escrow releasing funds only when milestones are verified.

      4. 04

        From insight to investment

        Banks, sovereign funds, impact capital and CSR programs connected to vetted food-security projects.

      Secure procurement rails

      Every tender step, on a tamper-evident record

      Every document, logistics event, and approval is recorded on a tamper-evident ledger for immediate auditability, and funds are released only when milestones are verified.

      {{LEDGER:RFQ published|TENDER-LINKED|Vetted bids|KYB VERIFIED|Contract|SMART CONTRACT|Delivery|MILESTONE VERIFIED|Payment|ESCROW RELEASE#A public tender passes from published RFQ to vetted bids, contract, verified delivery and escrow release. Each step is written as a block on a shared, tamper-evident record.}}

      Use case

      Stabilizing wheat supply during a regional shock

      The signal

      A mid-sized importing country faces early signs of disruption to its wheat supply as a key exporter announces potential export restrictions following a poor harvest. The AI-driven early-warning module has already flagged emerging reports of production shortfalls, giving the team valuable lead time.

      The response

      Officials open the surplus–deficit map to identify alternative origins, run scenarios in the policy sandbox, and publish an RFQ to vetted suppliers, linked to government-issued tender IDs and terms.

      The outcome

      Faster, cleaner procurement; moderated domestic price pressures; and a medium-term strategy to reduce vulnerability to similar shocks.

      FAQ

      Common questions

      How does T57 support national and regional food-security strategies in practice?

      Many countries are now expanding strategic reserves and silo capacity to hold months’ worth of essential commodities. T57 complements such physical infrastructure by tracking self-sufficiency, stock levels, and import exposure in real time. This combination of physical reserves and digital intelligence helps governments move from reactive to anticipatory food-security management.

      Why is it important to channel private and impact capital into agriculture and food systems, beyond public budgets?

      Despite agriculture’s historical role in employment and food security, global investors are only now seeking credible, measurable pathways to support food systems as part of their climate and SDG commitments. T57 helps governments present investable, data-backed opportunities, from model support centers to special agri zones and CSR programs, with transparent performance and impact tracking that meets both regulatory and investor expectations.

      Turn your food system into a governable, investable public asset.

      Use case

      Escrowed Malaysian rice trade with staged exposure

      The opportunity

      A regional investment platform wants short-duration exposure to essential food imports in Southeast Asia. Through T57 it reviews a rice supply opportunity linked to a government-supported procurement programme in Malaysia, with demand, counterparties and payment structures already assessed.

      The structure

      Instead of funding the full value at once, the investor commits a first tranche through escrow. Capital is released in stages against verified milestones: supplier confirmation, shipment progress and delivery documentation.

      Supplier confirmedShipment in progressDelivery documented

      Three tranches, each released after its milestone is verified.

      FAQ

      Common questions

      How does T57 handle disputes and reduce risks for financiers and investors?

      T57 reduces risk through its curated club membership model, which ensures vetted, credible counterparties in a high-trust environment. Its virtual trade desk supports execution, manages disputes, oversees documentation, and ensures consistent transaction follow-through for greater investor confidence.

      Why is food and agri finance an important opportunity for investors now?

      Global food import demand remains enormous: FAO puts the global food import bill at $2.22 trillion in 2025, which underlines the scale and persistence of trade-linked financing needs in food markets.

      Is trade finance generally considered a lower risk than other forms of credit exposure?

      Yes. The ICC Trade Register highlights that trade, supply chain, and export finance products continue to exhibit low-risk profiles and resilient default performance across challenging market conditions.

      Why do financiers need stronger diligence and monitoring tools in agri markets?

      Food and agri transactions often involve fragmented supply chains, cross-border counterparties, and climate or logistics volatility, which makes visibility and verification especially valuable. The International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) notes that small-scale producers remain underserved by finance, highlighting that large financing needs go unmet because risk gaps discourage capital.

      See finance-ready food and agri opportunities on T57.

      The challenge

      The real risk is not production. It is the buyer.

      Margins in food sales and exports are built, or broken, in procurement, documentation, payments and the quality of buyer relationships. T57 brings these parts together into a single, transparent environment.

      Unreliable buyers

      The real risk is not knowing if the buyer is genuine or likely to honor terms once the cargo is on the way. A single failed transaction can wipe out a season's profit.

      Fragmented documents and logistics

      Export paperwork is scattered across email, messaging apps and spreadsheets. One missing or inconsistent document can mean delays, demurrage or rejection.

      Price and payment uncertainty

      Volatile commodity prices and long payment cycles, where intermediaries can capture more than their own trading margin.

      Use case · Illustrative example

      Indian rice exporter scales faster with trusted trade infrastructure

      A mid-sized Golden Sella and Basmati rice exporter in India traditionally sold to a handful of known buyers in the Middle East, relying on brokers for both leads and collections. The exporter joined T57 as a club member and completed the KYB and capacity verification process.

      Using T57's price and market intelligence, the exporter identified strong demand–supply signals from Malaysia and East Africa and responded to RFQs from two new buyers, negotiating via T57's AI-assisted tools and locking each order into a smart contract with escrow and independent quality inspection. All documentation was generated and stored in a single order workspace, with automatic sharing with financiers and insurers.

      Within one season, the exporter expanded from one to three active markets, shortened its average payment cycle by more than two weeks, and reduced document-related disputes to near zero thanks to end-to-end traceability.

      Why T57

      Built by practitioners, not a generic marketplace

      T57 is built by people who have spent decades trading fresh produce, staples and high-value commodities across complex corridors.

      Trust layer

      Every party you meet on T57 has passed structured checks on ownership, financial behavior, capacity and on-ground operations.

      Evidence-based compliance

      Digital tools, logistics intelligence, granular documentation and impact metrics support evidence-based compliance that resonates with institutional partners.

      FAQ

      Questions sellers ask

      How does T57's virtual trade desk help in disputes and risk management?

      The virtual trade desk acts as a risk manager. In the event of disputes, the desk steps in to mediate, enforce agreed-upon terms and protect the seller's interests. If a buyer becomes insolvent or defaults, T57 shifts to a commission-based recovery and resale approach, helping redirect goods or recover value.

      How does a platform help with the financing gap?

      Dedicated trade platforms that provide rich transaction and compliance data can lower perceived risk for financiers, improving access to credit and reducing the cost of capital. T57 is designed to expose this data in an auditable way so that funders can underwrite your deals with greater confidence.

      Why is documentation and certification such a big issue in food exports?

      Food exports are subject to stringent import-country inspection and certification regimes. Incomplete or incorrect certification can lead to rejection or non-compliance at the border. A system that centralizes documents, links them to lots and shipments, and validates certifications reduces the risk of costly rejections and delays.

      Can better intelligence really help in volatile export markets?

      Agricultural prices remain exposed to extreme weather, changing biofuel policies and rising trade barriers. Exporters using structured market, crop and price intelligence are better able to adjust sourcing and pricing to protect margins.

      Ready to trade with more confidence?

      TodayWith T57

      Animated infographic: quotes and orders meet in one deal file, and lenders compete to fund it

      Run both sides of every deal on one record, and fund it faster

      Traders make food trade work. They find supply, bundle volumes, take on risk and move goods across borders. T57 brings your suppliers, buyers, finance and logistics onto one verified record.

      The challenge

      Traders carry both sides of the risk, often on their own balance sheet

      Lenders cannot see a clean record of the trade. Banks rejected 41% of SME trade finance applications in 2025, and the global trade finance gap reached $2.5 trillion (ADB, January 2026).

      Tied-up capital

      Traders often pay suppliers before buyers pay them, which limits how many deals they can run.

      Two-sided risk

      A failure by the supplier or the buyer lands on the trader, and paperwork rarely lines up across both.

      Trust deficit

      Intermediaries are sometimes seen as adding cost without value, so honest traders need a way to prove theirs.

      How T57 works for you

      From verified profile to a funded, executed deal

      FAQ

      Common questions

      Can intermediaries join T57?

      Yes. Traders and intermediaries are welcome. They are labelled by role so every counterparty knows how the trade is structured.

      Does T57 lend to traders?

      No. T57 does not lend. It sends your deal file to licensed lenders, who decide whether to fund the trade and on what terms.

      How do back-to-back contracts work on T57?

      The supplier's accepted quote and the buyer's accepted order each generate a contract, and both sit on the same trade record so terms stay consistent.

      What does a track record show?

      Your completed trades, verification status and role, so new counterparties and lenders can see your history before they deal with you.

      The challenge

      Buying from suppliers you cannot fully check

      Food importers carry the most risk in a trade. They often pay before goods arrive, rely on documents they cannot easily verify and deal with suppliers they have never met.       Supplier uncertainty

      It is hard to tell whether a supplier is the producer, a processor or one more intermediary adding cost.

      Quality and documentation risk

      Certificates, inspection reports and contracts arrive from different sources and do not always match.

      Payment and supply risk

      Paying upfront exposes buyers to fraud and delay, while single-source supply leaves them exposed to shocks.

      Use case · Illustrative example

      Indian FPO scales local brand through contract-backed exports

      A vegetable FPO in Maharashtra, India, aggregates produce from more than 800 smallholder members and has built a modest local brand, but it primarily sells to regional wholesalers at fluctuating spot prices. Despite its infrastructure and membership, the FPO struggles to secure institutional contracts or access export buyers because it lacks market intelligence, tendering experience, and structured finance.

      After onboarding to T57, the FPO publishes its seasonal production plan and uses AI-driven trade matchmaking to identify buyers seeking traceable vegetables. Through RFQ bidding, it responds to a supermarket chain's regional sourcing tender and a Gulf-based importer's contract opportunity, with support from T57's virtual trade desk. With trade finance from partner banks, the FPO secures pre-shipment funding, routes payments through escrow, and uses T57's document and logistics tools to manage export-ready consignments. Over two seasons, its members experience more predictable prices, improved cash flow, and stronger demand for the FPO's own brand.

      FAQ

      Common questions

      Why should a farmer or producer use a digital trade platform like T57?

      T57 provides access to verified buyers and transparent payment processes. This reduces uncertainty and improves income realization.

      What should farmers watch out for in contract farming?

      Contract farming deals are often between stronger buyers and weaker farmers. This could result in unfair terms, over-dependence on a single buyer, or disputes over quality and deductions. Farmers can access T57's expertise to negotiate the best terms.

      Can better market access really reduce waste?

      Yes. Better matching of supply with demand, along with more coordinated trade execution, can reduce losses between harvest and market.

      Why is finance such a major issue for producers?

      The World Bank notes that agriculture finance remains disproportionately limited in many developing markets due to risk, transaction costs, and the difficulty of serving fragmented rural borrowers. That is why trade-linked and digitally enabled finance models matter for producers who need working capital tied to real orders.

      Does price intelligence really matter at the farm level?

      Yes. When producers lack visibility into demand and prices, they negotiate from a weaker position and often rely too heavily on intermediaries. T57's core model directly addresses this by improving access to market and price intelligence.
